definition_zh: （名词）词缀；附加物；（动词）附上；粘贴；盖（印）
definition_en: a letter or letters added to a word to form a new word; to attach or fasten something to a surface
core_image: 一枚被贴上去的小标签：附在词根或物体上
scene: 旧书摊的桌上放着一叠信封，摊主正把一枚邮票按在右上角。He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 affixed 是「贴上、粘上」（第 3 个义项：把某物固定到另一物表面）；句意为他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。画面中可辨识：旧书摊、信封、邮票。

pos.zh: 词缀；附加物
附上；粘贴；盖（印）

derivatives.zh: 由 affix 加 -ation 构成，义为「词缀法；附加过程」
由 affix 加 -al 构成，义为「词缀的；与词缀有关的」

senses.title: A word element added to a root
senses.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word to change its meaning or form
senses.definitionCN: 加在词首或词尾、用以改变词义或词形的字母或字母组合
senses.example: The prefix un- is a common affix in English.
senses.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 是英语中常见的词缀。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the physical verb: a prefix or suffix is fastened onto a root just as a label is fastened onto a box.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个物理动词：前缀或后缀就像标签贴到盒子上一样，被固定在词根上。

senses.title: Something attached as an addition
senses.definition: a thing attached or added to something else, often as a minor addition
senses.definitionCN: 附加或添加到另一物上的东西，常指次要的添加物
senses.example: The contract had a short affix listing two extra duties.
senses.exampleCN: 合同后面附了一份简短的附加条款，列出两项额外义务。
senses.why: The noun keeps the literal sense: whatever has been fastened on becomes an affix.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了字面义：凡是被固定上去的东西，就成为一个 affix。

senses.title: To attach or fasten to a surface
senses.definition: to attach, fasten, or stick something onto a surface or object
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附着、固定或粘贴到某个表面或物体上
senses.example: He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。
senses.why: The Latin past participle meant fastened to, and the verb still means exactly that, with no metaphor needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语过去分词意为「固定于」，这个动词至今仍是这个意思，完全不需要比喻。

senses.title: To add a signature or seal
senses.definition: to add a signature, seal, or mark to a document in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上正式加上签名、印章或标记
senses.example: Both parties affixed their seals to the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都在协议上盖了章。
senses.why: A seal is literally pressed onto paper, so this official sense is only the physical act made legal.
senses.whyCN: 印章确实是压在纸上的，所以这个正式义只是把物理动作放进了法律程序。

intro.en: Affix comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to fasten to', and its grammatical sense is a later borrowing of that physical image.
intro.cn: affix 来自拉丁语动词「固定到」，其语法义是后来从这个物理意象借来的。

items.en: Figere meant 'to fasten, fix, drive in', and it also gave English fix.
items.cn: figere 意为「固定、钉入」，它也给了英语 fix 这个词。

items.en: Affigere meant 'to fasten to, attach', built from ad- and figere.
items.cn: affigere 意为「固定到、附上」，由 ad- 与 figere 构成。

items.en: The past participle affixus meant 'fastened to' and became the English noun and adjective stem.
items.cn: 过去分词 affixus 意为「固定于」，成为英语名词与形容词的词干。

items.en: English used affix first for a thing fastened on, then adopted it for word elements in grammar.
items.cn: 英语先用 affix 指被固定上去的东西，后来在语法中用它指词缀。

items.en: Affixation became the standard term for the process of adding prefixes and suffixes.
items.cn: affixation 成为表示添加前缀与后缀这一过程的标准术语。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the same 'fasten' root; the second gathers word-formation and attachment terms.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「固定」词根的一族词；第二组收构词与附着类术语。

entries.definition: The process of adding an affix to a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词缀法；附加过程」，由 affix 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to an affix or to affixes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「词缀的」，由 affix 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To repair something or fasten it in place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修理；固定」，与 affix 同出拉丁语 figere「固定」。

entries.definition: An affix added to the beginning of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词首。

entries.definition: An affix added to the end of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词尾。

entries.definition: Something fastened or joined to another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附着物」，与义项二相近，但更强调连接关系。

normalIntro.en: Affix is best held by the word fix: an affix is something fixed onto something else.
normalIntro.cn: affix 可以靠 fix 这个词来记：affix 就是被固定到别处的东西。

normal.en: Fix means fasten, and af- is the assimilated form of ad-, so affix is to fasten to.
normal.cn: fix 意为「固定」，af- 是 ad- 的同化形式，所以 affix 就是「固定到」。

normal.en: A prefix is an affix at the front and a suffix is an affix at the end.
normal.cn: prefix 是位于词首的 affix，suffix 是位于词尾的 affix。

normal.en: To affix a stamp is the everyday physical use that keeps the original image alive.
normal.cn: affix a stamp「贴邮票」是让原始意象保持鲜活的日常用法。

normal.en: Affixation names the process, and affixal describes anything about affixes.
normal.cn: affixation 指这个过程，affixal 描述与词缀有关的事物。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, while the verb is often unstressed differently.
normal.cn: 名词重音落在第一个音节，动词的读法常常不同。

abstract.en: Picture a small sticker pressed onto the corner of a page, easy to miss but impossible to remove without a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小贴纸压在书页角上，容易忽略，却一撕就会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Think of a word as a body and an affix as a piece of clothing put on at the edge.
abstract.cn: 把一个词想成身体，把词缀想成穿在边缘的一件衣服。

abstract.en: See the same hand that fixes a stamp also fixing meaning onto a root.
abstract.cn: 想象贴邮票的那只手，也在把意义固定到词根上。

examples.en: The affix -ness turns adjectives into nouns.
examples.cn: 词缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

examples.en: Please affix your signature to the bottom of the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。

examples.en: The parcel had no return address on it.
examples.cn: 包裹上没有寄件人的地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲克斯」——阿（a）菲（fei）克（ke）斯（si），把东西固定上去，就像词缀贴在词根上。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 figere「固定」构成 affigere「固定到」，过去分词 affixus 成为英语的 affix；作动词时读「/əˈfɪks/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a physical act of fastening, then splits into the thing fastened on and the grammar term for letters fastened to a root.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初是物理上的「固定」动作，随后分成两条线：被固定上去的东西，以及语法中固定在词根上的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small label pressed onto a surface
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚压在某物表面的小标签

branches.en: Letters fastened to a root to make a new word.
branches.cn: 固定在词根上以构成新词的字母。

branches.en: Any object fastened on as an addition.
branches.cn: 作为附加物固定上去的任何物件。

branches.en: The physical act of sticking something on.
branches.cn: 把某物贴上去的物理动作。

branches.en: A seal or signature pressed onto a document.
branches.cn: 压在文件上的印章或签名。

branches.en: Everyday sticking and formal sealing as one action.
branches.cn: 日常粘贴与正式盖章是同一个动作。

intro.en: Affix is a Latin verb form that became both a noun and a verb in English, with a small but clear family.
intro.cn: affix 是拉丁语动词形式，在英语中同时成为名词与动词，词族不大却清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus figere produced affigere, whose participle affixus English borrowed directly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 figere 构成 affigere，英语直接借用了它的分词形式 affixus。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

latinEntries.example: Figere also gave English fix.
latinEntries.exampleCN: figere 也给了英语 fix。

latinEntries.example: Affixus became the English affix.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affixus 成为英语的 affix。

definition_zh: 折磨；使痛苦；使苦恼；（疾病）侵袭
definition_en: to cause pain, suffering, or distress to someone, often repeatedly or over a long period
core_image: 一记反复落下的打击，让人长期受苦
scene: 雨季里，村庄的道路被洪水冲断，病人要走很远才能找到医生。Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
sceneCN: 这里 afflicted 是「折磨、使受苦」（第 1 个义项：给身体或精神带来持续痛苦）；句意为慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。画面中可辨识：被冲断的道路、拄杖的病人、远处的诊所。

pos.zh: 折磨；使痛苦；（疾病）侵袭

derivatives.zh: 由 afflict 加 -ion 构成，义为「痛苦；苦难；折磨人的病痛」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「受折磨的；患病的」
由 afflict 加 -ive 构成，义为「令人痛苦的；造成苦难的」

senses.title: To cause pain or suffering
senses.definition: to cause pain or suffering to a person or group, especially over time
senses.definitionCN: 给人或群体带来痛苦或苦难，尤指持续性的
senses.example: Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to strike something down, so suffering is pictured as blow after blow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「击倒」，所以苦难被想象成一记接一记的打击。

senses.title: Of a disease: to attack
senses.definition: of an illness or condition, to attack a person or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或病症侵袭某人或身体某部位
senses.example: A rare skin disease afflicted the workers in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 一种罕见的皮肤病侵袭了那座旧工厂里的工人。
senses.why: A disease arrives like a series of blows the body cannot ward off, which is why the verb fits illness so well.
senses.whyCN: 疾病到来就像身体挡不住的一连串打击，所以这个动词特别适合描述疾病。

senses.title: To bring hardship to a place or group
senses.definition: to cause hardship, disaster, or serious difficulty for a place or community
senses.definitionCN: 给某地或某群体带来困苦、灾难或严重困难
senses.example: Drought and failed harvests afflicted the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱和歉收让整个地区陷入苦难。
senses.why: The blows can fall on a whole community, not only on one body, so the word extends to shared hardship.
senses.whyCN: 打击可以落在整个社区而不只是一个人身上，于是这个词扩展到共同的苦难。

senses.title: To trouble the mind
senses.definition: to distress or trouble someone mentally, especially with worry or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 在精神上使某人痛苦或困扰，尤指忧虑与疑虑
senses.example: Doubts about the decision afflicted her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个决定的疑虑折磨了她好几个星期。
senses.why: What strikes the body can also strike the mind, and this sense names the inward version of the same pain.
senses.whyCN: 打击身体的东西也能打击心灵，这个义项指的是同一种痛苦转向内心的形态。

intro.en: Afflict comes from Latin verbs of striking, and its core image is a blow that keeps falling.
intro.cn: afflict 来自拉丁语表示「打击」的动词，核心意象是一记不断落下的打击。

items.en: Fligere meant 'to strike, dash', and it also lies behind conflict.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击、猛撞」，它也是 conflict 的词源成分。

items.en: Affligere meant 'to dash down, strike against, ruin', built with ad- and fligere.
items.cn: affligere 意为「击倒、撞击、毁坏」，由 ad- 与 fligere 构成。

items.en: The frequentative afflictare meant 'to keep striking, harass, torment'.
items.cn: 反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断打击、骚扰、折磨」。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin participle afflictus, partly through French, as the verb afflict.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入拉丁语分词 afflictus，形成动词 afflict。

items.en: The medical and mental senses settled beside the older sense of external hardship.
items.cn: 医学义与精神义在较早的「外在困苦」义旁稳定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'strike' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of causing pain and hardship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「打击」词根的一族词；近义组收造成痛苦与困苦的动词。

entries.definition: A condition of pain, suffering, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「痛苦；苦难；病痛」，由 afflict 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Suffering from pain, illness, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受折磨的；患病的」，是 afflict 的过去分词。

entries.definition: A serious disagreement or a fight between opposing forces.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲突；争斗」，与 afflict 同出拉丁语 fligere「打击」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone severe and lasting suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「折磨」，痛苦程度比 afflict 更重，常带持续性。

entries.definition: To cause continual trouble or distress to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不断困扰；使遭灾」，强调反复与恼人。

entries.definition: To make someone feel very worried, unhappy, or uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使痛苦；使忧虑」，侧重情绪上的难受。

normalIntro.en: Afflict is held by the image of a strike and by its large family of nouns and adjectives.
normalIntro.cn: afflict 可以靠「打击」这个意象，以及它成串的名词与形容词来记。

normal.en: Fligere means strike, so afflict is to strike someone down with pain.
normal.cn: fligere 意为「打击」，所以 afflict 就是用痛苦把人击倒。

normal.en: Affliction is the pain itself, and afflicted describes the person who carries it.
normal.cn: affliction 是痛苦本身，afflicted 描述承受痛苦的人。

normal.en: Be afflicted with is the passive phrase used for illness and hardship.
normal.cn: be afflicted with 是用于疾病与困苦的被动搭配。

normal.en: Conflict shares the same strike root but adds a different prefix meaning together.
normal.cn: conflict 共享同一「打击」词根，只是前缀表示「共同」。

normal.en: Afflictive is the adjective for whatever causes the suffering.
normal.cn: afflictive 是形容造成痛苦之物的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer that keeps falling on the same spot, never quite stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锤子反复落在同一个地方，始终停不下来。

abstract.en: Think of a weight carried on the shoulders for years, invisible to others.
abstract.cn: 想象一副在肩上压了多年的重担，别人却看不见。

abstract.en: See the word as rain that will not stop: at first it is weather, then it becomes hardship.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一场停不下来的雨：起初只是天气，后来就成了苦难。

examples.en: The region has been afflicted by drought for three years.
examples.cn: 这个地区已经遭受旱灾三年。

examples.en: She was afflicted with a severe headache before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她饱受剧烈头痛的折磨。

examples.en: The village rebuilt its bridge the following spring.
examples.cn: 村庄在第二年春天重建了桥梁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗利克特」——阿（a）弗（fu）利（li）克（ke）特（te），一记记打击不断落在身上。

root: 拉丁语 fligere「打击」加前缀 ad- 构成 affligere「击倒」，其反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断折磨」，英语借入分词形式 afflictus。

sensesIntro.en: One image of repeated blows expands outward: physical pain, disease, communal hardship, and finally mental trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 「反复打击」这一意象向外扩展：身体疼痛、疾病、群体困苦，最后是精神上的困扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blow after blow falling on the same spot
core.cn: 核心意象：一记接一记落在同一处的打击

branches.en: Pain pictured as repeated blows.
branches.cn: 把痛苦想象成反复的打击。

branches.en: A disease delivering those blows.
branches.cn: 疾病送来这些打击。

branches.en: The blows landing on a whole community.
branches.cn: 打击落在整个社区身上。

branches.en: The same blows turned inward on the mind.
branches.cn: 同样的打击转向内心。

branches.en: Pain for one body and hardship for a group.
branches.cn: 一个人的疼痛与一群人的困苦。

intro.en: Afflict is built from a prefix and a Latin root of striking, and its family is mostly suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: afflict 由前缀与表示「打击」的拉丁词根构成，其词族主要是同一词干加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fligere gave affligere, and the participle afflictus gave English its stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fligere 构成 affligere，分词 afflictus 为英语提供了词干。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fligere is the root of afflict and conflict.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fligere 是 afflict 与 conflict 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Afflictare strengthened the sense of repeated pain.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afflictare 强化了反复痛苦的含义。

definition_zh: 富裕；富足；（人、货物或水的）大量涌入
definition_en: the state of having a great deal of money and material comfort; in older use, an abundant inward flow of people, goods or water
core_image: 财富像水一样不断流进来
scene: 这条街十年前只有几家小店，如今橱窗一间接一间亮起来。Affluence has reshaped the whole neighbourhood.
sceneCN: 这里 affluence 是「富裕」（第 1 个义项：财富充裕、生活舒适的状态）；句意为富裕改变了整个街区的面貌。核心画面是财富像水一样不断流进来。

pos.zh: 富裕；富足；涌入

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ence 换 -ent 的形容词，义为「富裕的；富足的」
affluent 加 -ly，义为「富足地；充裕地」
同根名词，义为「（人、物的）流入；汇集」

senses.title: A state of having plenty of money
senses.definition: the condition of having a great deal of money, property and material comfort
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱、财产与物质享受的状态
senses.example: Two decades of growth brought affluence to the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的增长让沿海城镇富裕起来。
senses.why: Ad- means toward and fluere means to flow, so affluence is literally a flowing-toward: wealth keeps arriving instead of sitting still.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示「朝向」，fluere 表示「流动」，所以 affluence 字面就是「朝……流来」：财富不断涌来，而不是静止不动。

senses.title: A large inward flow of people or things
senses.definition: an abundant incoming stream of people, goods or water, the older and more literal sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 人、货物或水大量流入的情形，是该词更古老、更字面的用法
senses.example: The affluence of visitors strained the little station.
senses.exampleCN: 游客的大量涌入让这个小车站不堪重负。
senses.why: This keeps the original river image intact: the word first described water flowing in, and money later borrowed that picture.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留了最初的河流意象：该词最早描述水的流入，后来金钱借用了这幅画面。

intro.en: Affluence is a river word that became a money word: Latin ad-, toward, plus fluere, to flow, gives a flowing-in, and English used it of water long before it used it of wealth.
intro.cn: affluence 是一个从河流变成金钱的词：拉丁语 ad-「朝向」加 fluere「流动」构成「流入」，英语先用于水，很久以后才用于财富。

items.en: Latin ad meant to or toward, and it assimilates to af- before an f, which is why the word is spelled with a double f.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad 意为「向、朝」，在 f 前同化为 af-，这正是该词拼作双写 f 的原因。

items.en: Latin fluere meant to flow, the root behind fluent, fluid, influence and flush.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fluere 意为「流动」，是 fluent、fluid、influence 与 flush 背后的词根。

items.en: Combining the two gave affluere, to flow toward, used of rivers running into a larger body of water.
items.cn: 两者结合得到 affluere「朝……流来」，用于描述河流汇入更大的水体。

items.en: The noun affluentia named abundance and a plentiful inflow, already carrying the sense of plenty.
items.cn: 名词 affluentia 表示丰裕与大量流入，已经带有「充足」的意味。

items.en: Old French affluence kept both the flow and the abundance senses, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 affluence 同时保留「流动」与「丰裕」两义，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: By the twentieth century English affluence meant chiefly material wealth, and the phrase the affluent society made that meaning dominant.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，英语 affluence 主要指物质财富，the affluent society 这一说法让该义成为主流。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the flu- family of flowing; the near-meaning group lists other words for having plenty of money.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「流动」的 flu- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「有钱」的词。

entries.definition: Having a great deal of money and a comfortable standard of living.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱与舒适生活水平的。

entries.definition: The power to shape what someone thinks or does.
entries.definitionCN: 影响他人想法或行为的力量。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers join and flow together.
entries.definitionCN: 两条河流汇合之处。

entries.definition: Liquid waste flowing out of a factory or works.
entries.definitionCN: 从工厂流出的液体废物。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and valuable possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 大量金钱与贵重财产。

entries.definition: The state of being successful, especially in making money.
entries.definitionCN: 成功兴旺的状态，尤指赚钱方面。

entries.definition: Great wealth shown off through expensive surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 通过奢华环境显示出来的巨大财富。

entries.definition: A quantity that is more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 多得用不完的数量。

normalIntro.en: Affluence is af-, toward, plus flu, flow, plus -ence, a state: the state of wealth flowing toward you.
normalIntro.cn: affluence 就是 af-「朝向」加 flu「流」加 -ence「状态」：财富朝你流来的状态。

normal.en: Flu means flow, so affluent, influence and confluence all keep something moving.
normal.cn: flu 表示流动，所以 affluent、influence、confluence 都让某物保持流动。

normal.en: The double f is ad- turning into af- before fluere, the same change as in afford and afflict.
normal.cn: 双写 f 是 ad- 在 fluere 前变成 af-，与 afford、afflict 中的变化相同。

normal.en: Money that flows in is affluence; money that flows out is expenditure.
normal.cn: 流进来的钱是 affluence，流出去的钱是 expenditure。

normal.en: -ence marks a state, as in silence and presence, so affluence is the state of flowing in.
normal.cn: -ence 表示状态，如 silence、presence，所以 affluence 就是「流入」的状态。

normal.en: Affluence is usually uncountable, so write growing affluence, not an affluence.
normal.cn: affluence 通常不可数，所以写 growing affluence，不写 an affluence。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running downhill into your courtyard and never stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币的河顺坡流进你的院子，从不停下。

abstract.en: Imagine a tide that comes in but never goes out, leaving the shore deep in goods.
abstract.cn: 想象一道只涨不退的潮，把岸边堆满货物。

abstract.en: Think of a reservoir whose inflow pipe is wider than its outlet.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水库，进水管比出水管还粗。

examples.en: The report links rising affluence to longer life expectancy.
examples.cn: 报告把日益富裕与更长的预期寿命联系起来。

examples.en: Affluence did not reach every village in the valley.
examples.cn: 富裕并未惠及山谷里的每一个村庄。

examples.en: They grew up in affluence but learned to budget carefully.
examples.cn: 他们在富足中长大，却学会了精打细算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福路恩思」——阿福（af）走的那条路（flu）上恩（ence）泽不断，钱像水一样流进来，就是富裕、富足。

root: 拉丁语前缀 ad-「朝向」在 f 前同化为 af-，加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「朝……流来」，其名词 affluentia 经古法语 affluence 进入英语，字面即「不断流入的丰裕」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same inflow: the older one counts water and people arriving, the newer one counts money arriving, and in each case plenty keeps coming in.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种流入：较早的义项数的是流来的水与人，较新的义项数的是流来的钱，两者都是丰裕不断涌来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wealth flowing in like water
core.cn: 核心意象：财富像水一样流进来

branches.en: Money arriving year after year.
branches.cn: 金钱年复一年地涌来。

branches.en: Comfort that lasts because the inflow never stops.
branches.cn: 因为流入不停而长久留存的舒适。

branches.en: A crowd pouring into one small place.
branches.cn: 人群涌进一个小地方。

branches.en: Rivers running into a larger stream.
branches.cn: 河流汇入更大的水流。

branches.en: Both measure abundance by how much flows in.
branches.cn: 两者都用流入量来衡量丰裕。

intro.en: Affluence sits in the flu- family, where the root always means flow and the prefix decides which direction the flow takes.
intro.cn: affluence 属于 flu- 词族，词根永远表示流动，前缀决定流动的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad plus fluere gave affluere and the noun affluentia, which French passed on to English almost unchanged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad 加 fluere 构成 affluere 与名词 affluentia，法语几乎原样把它传给英语。

latinEntries.example: Ad becomes af- before f.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ad 在 f 前变为 af-。

latinEntries.example: Fluere gives flu- in many English words.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 为许多英语词提供 flu-。

latinEntries.example: Affluere described rivers joining a larger water.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluere 描述河流汇入更大的水体。

latinEntries.example: Affluentia is the direct source of affluence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluentia 是 affluence 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 富裕的；富足的；（地区）高档的；丰富的
definition_en: having a lot of money and a high standard of living; plentiful or abundant
core_image: 水源源不断流进来的样子：钱与资源充盈
scene: 河岸边的山坡上，新盖的房子一栋接一栋，花园里种着整齐的树。The affluent suburb has large houses, private schools, and quiet streets.
sceneCN: 这里 affluent 是「富裕的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财、生活水准高）；句意为这个富裕的郊区有大房子、私立学校和安静的街道。画面中可辨识：山坡住宅、花园、安静的街道。

pos.zh: 富裕的；富足的；丰富的
富裕人群（the affluent）

derivatives.zh: 由 affluent 去掉词尾加 -ence 构成，义为「富裕；丰裕」
由 affluent 加 -ly 构成，义为「富裕地；丰足地」
由 affluent 与 influenza 缩合而成，指过度追求物质带来的「富裕病」，属非正式用词

senses.title: Having plenty of money
senses.definition: having a great deal of money and a high standard of living
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财、生活水准很高
senses.example: The affluent couple donated a large sum to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 这对富裕的夫妇向图书馆捐了一大笔钱。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to flow toward, and the image is resources flowing in without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「流向」，意象是资源不停地流进来。

senses.title: Of a place: wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: of an area or neighbourhood, inhabited by wealthy people and offering expensive services
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或街区住着富裕人群、提供昂贵服务
senses.example: They moved to an affluent suburb with a private school nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到了一个附近有私立学校的富裕郊区。
senses.why: Wealth spreads across a map: when many rich households cluster, the place itself is called affluent.
senses.whyCN: 财富会铺到地图上：当许多富裕家庭聚集，这个地方本身就被称为 affluent。

senses.title: Existing in abundance
senses.definition: present in large quantities; plentiful, used especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 大量存在的、充裕的，尤用于正式书面语
senses.example: The valley had affluent supplies of water and timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷拥有充裕的水源和木材。
senses.why: The original sense was simply flowing plentifully, before money narrowed the word in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思只是「大量流动」，在日常生活里才被钱的意义收窄。

senses.title: Flowing freely, in older use
senses.definition: flowing freely or in abundance, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 自由地或大量地流动，这一义项较古老，现今罕用
senses.example: The old poem describes an affluent stream that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗描写一条永不干涸的丰沛溪流。
senses.why: Before it named money, the word described water moving in quantity; that literal sense survives mainly in old texts.
senses.whyCN: 在指钱之前，这个词描述的是大量流动的水；这一字面义主要残留在旧文本里。

intro.en: Affluent is built on a Latin verb for flowing, and wealth was originally pictured as a flow of resources.
intro.cn: affluent 建立在拉丁语表示「流动」的动词上，财富最初被想象成资源的流动。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow', and it also gave English fluent and fluid.
items.cn: fluere 意为「流动」，它也给了英语 fluent 与 fluid。

items.en: Affluere meant 'to flow to, to flow in abundance', built with ad- and fluere.
items.cn: affluere 意为「流向、大量涌入」，由 ad- 与 fluere 构成。

items.en: Affluentia named abundance and the flow of wealth or supplies.
items.cn: affluentia 指丰裕，以及财富或物资的流入。

items.en: English first used affluent for flowing abundantly, then for people with abundant means.
items.cn: 英语最初用 affluent 表示「大量流动」，后来才指拥有丰裕资财的人。

items.en: The wealth sense became dominant, while the literal water sense retreated to older texts.
items.cn: 财富义成为主流，字面的水流义退回到旧文本中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'flow' root; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「流动」词根的一族词；近义组收表示财富与富足生活的词。

entries.definition: A state of having a lot of money and material goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕；丰裕」，是 affluent 的名词形式。

entries.definition: Able to speak or write a language easily and smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流利的」，与 affluent 同出拉丁语 fluere「流动」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers flow together, or a coming together of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汇流处；汇集」，同样来自 fluere「流动」。

entries.definition: Having a large amount of money, property, or valuable things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有的」，与 affluent 义项一几乎同义，更直白。

entries.definition: Successful and financially strong, especially of a person or region.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「繁荣的；兴旺的」，侧重发展与成功，而非单纯拥有钱财。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live comfortably.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的；日子好过的」，程度比 affluent 温和。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts, more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的；大量的」，对应义项三，但不含财富义。

normalIntro.en: Affluent is anchored by the root flu, which means flow, and by the picture of money flowing in.
normalIntro.cn: affluent 可以靠表示「流动」的词根 flu，以及钱不断流入的画面来记。

normal.en: Flu means flow, and affluere means to flow toward, so affluent is 'flowing in with resources'.
normal.cn: flu 意为「流动」，affluere 意为「流向」，所以 affluent 就是「资源源源流入」。

normal.en: Affluence is the noun for the state, and affluently is the adverb.
normal.cn: affluence 是表示状态的名词，affluently 是副词。

normal.en: An affluent suburb is a place where wealthy households cluster.
normal.cn: affluent suburb 是富裕家庭聚集的地方。

normal.en: Fluent and fluid share the same root, which keeps the flow image in view.
normal.cn: fluent 与 fluid 共享同一词根，让「流动」的意象始终可见。

normal.en: The phrase the affluent treats the adjective as a collective noun.
normal.cn: 「the affluent」这个说法把形容词当作集合名词使用。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running past a house and never running dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币组成的河从房前流过，永不干涸。

abstract.en: Think of a garden where the sprinkler is always on and the soil is always dark with water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，喷头一直开着，土壤总是被水浸得发黑。

abstract.en: See wealth as a current rather than a pile: what matters is how much keeps arriving.
abstract.cn: 把财富看成水流而不是堆叠：重要的是有多少在不断到来。

examples.en: The affluent neighbourhood has its own marina and tennis club.
examples.cn: 这个富裕的街区有自己的游艇码头和网球俱乐部。

examples.en: Affluent families often spend more on tutoring than on holidays.
examples.cn: 富裕家庭花在辅导上的钱常常比花在度假上的更多。

examples.en: The river ran clear after the spring rains.
examples.cn: 春雨过后，河水清澈地流着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗伦特」——阿（a）弗（fu）伦（lun）特（te），钱像水一样不断流进来，日子就富裕了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「流入、丰沛」，其名词 affluentia 指丰裕；英语先指「大量流动」，后专指富裕。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as water flowing in abundance, then narrows to money, then widens again to rich places and plentiful supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指水大量流动，后收窄为钱财，再扩展为富裕地区与充裕物资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: resources flowing in like a stream
core.cn: 核心意象：资源像溪流一样不断流入

branches.en: Money flowing into a household.
branches.cn: 钱财流入家庭。

branches.en: Wealth written across a whole district.
branches.cn: 财富铺展在整个街区。

branches.en: Supplies present in large quantity.
branches.cn: 大量存在的物资。

branches.en: The old literal sense of water flowing freely.
branches.cn: 水流自由流动的古老字面义。

branches.en: Abundance in money and abundance in goods.
branches.cn: 钱财的丰裕与物资的丰裕。

intro.en: Affluent is a prefix plus the Latin root for flow, with a family that spreads across several everyday words.
intro.cn: affluent 是前缀加拉丁语「流动」词根，其词族分布在好几个日常词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fluere made affluere, and fluentia supplied the noun affluence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fluere 构成 affluere，fluentia 则提供了名词 affluence。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fluere is the root of affluent and fluent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 是 affluent 与 fluent 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affluentia gave English affluence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluentia 给了英语 affluence。

definition_zh: 买得起；负担得起；有条件（做）；提供；给予
definition_en: to have enough money or resources for something; to be able to do something without serious risk; to provide or give something
core_image: 口袋里有足够的余量，能把这件事承担下来
scene: 月底的餐桌上，父母对着账单算了很久，最后还是决定让孩子去参加那次远行。They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
sceneCN: 这里 afford 是「负担得起」（第 1 个义项：有钱支付某事物的费用）；句意为那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。画面中可辨识：餐桌、账单、旅行宣传单。

pos.zh: 买得起；负担得起；提供；给予

derivatives.zh: 由 afford 加 -able 构成，义为「负担得起的；价格合理的」
由 affordable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性；价格可承受程度」

senses.title: To have enough money for something
senses.definition: to have enough money to pay for something without ruinous difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱支付某事物，而不至于造成严重困难
senses.example: They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。
senses.why: The old English word meant to further or accomplish, and the modern sense asks whether your means can carry the plan through.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词意为「推进、完成」，现代义则是在问你的财力能否把这件计划办成。

senses.title: To be in a position to do something
senses.definition: to be able to do something without serious risk or loss, often used with time or energy
senses.definitionCN: 能够做某事而不冒严重风险或损失，常与时间、精力连用
senses.example: We cannot afford to waste another week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们耗不起再浪费一个星期。
senses.why: Means are not only money: time and strength are also budgets, and the verb asks whether you can spare them.
senses.whyCN: 可支配的不只是钱：时间和精力也是预算，这个动词在问你是否抽得出。

senses.title: To provide or give
senses.definition: to provide or give something such as an opportunity, protection, or pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 提供机会、保护或乐趣等事物
senses.example: The quiet garden afforded him a place to think.
senses.exampleCN: 这座安静的花园给了他一个思考的地方。
senses.why: If your means can carry a plan, they can also yield something for others, so the verb extends to giving.
senses.whyCN: 如果你的财力能托起一项计划，它也能为别人产出些什么，于是这个动词扩展到「给予」。

senses.title: To bear the risk or consequence
senses.definition: to be able to accept the cost, risk, or consequence of an action
senses.definitionCN: 能够承受某项行动带来的代价、风险或后果
senses.example: The company cannot afford another failed launch.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司承受不起又一次失败的发布。
senses.why: This is the money sense grown abstract: what you can carry includes bad outcomes, not only bills.
senses.whyCN: 这是钱财义的抽象化：你能承担的东西也包括坏结果，而不只是账单。

intro.en: Afford is a native English word, not a Latin borrowing, and its early sense was to accomplish or further something.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语借词，早期意思是「完成、推进」某事。

items.en: Forth meant 'forward, onward', and it survives in English phrases such as bring forth.
items.cn: forth 意为「向前、往外」，还保留在 bring forth 等英语说法里。

items.en: Geforthian meant 'to further, promote, accomplish', built on the same forward idea.
items.cn: geforthian 意为「推进、促进、完成」，建立在同一个「向前」的概念上。

items.en: The verb weakened to aforthen, with senses of managing, supplying, and being able to meet a cost.
items.cn: 这个动词弱化为 aforthen，带有「设法办到、供给、付得起」等意思。

items.en: The modern spelling afford settled, and the sense 'have the means for' became central.
items.cn: 现代拼写 afford 固定下来，「有财力做某事」成为核心义。

items.en: Affordable and affordability grew into everyday words in housing, health care, and shopping.
items.cn: affordable 与 affordability 成为住房、医疗与购物语境中的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own derivatives and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of managing, providing, and bearing cost.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生词与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收支付、提供与承受代价类动词。

entries.definition: Cheap enough for most people to pay for.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的」，由 afford 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The degree to which something can be paid for by ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性」，指普通人能否支付得起。

entries.definition: A shallow place in a river where you can walk across.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浅滩；可涉水而过之处」；只是拼写与 afford 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To succeed in doing something despite difficulty, often with limited means.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法做到」，与义项二相近，强调在困难中仍能办成。

entries.definition: To give someone something they need or want.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提供；供给」，对应义项三，但不含支付能力的意思。

entries.definition: To accept or endure a cost, burden, or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担；承受」，与义项四相近，更强调忍受重量。

normalIntro.en: Afford is a native word tied to 'forward', and it is best held by the phrase can afford.
normalIntro.cn: afford 是与「向前」相关的本族词，最好借 can afford 这个说法来记。

normal.en: The old word meant to further a plan, so affording something is carrying the plan through.
normal.cn: 这个古词意为推进计划，所以 afford 某物就是把计划托着办下去。

normal.en: Can afford is the common frame, and it asks whether your means can bear the cost.
normal.cn: can afford 是常见框架，问的是你的财力能否承担这笔费用。

normal.en: Afford to do extends the idea from money to time, energy, and risk.
normal.cn: afford to do 把这个概念从钱扩展到时间、精力与风险。

normal.en: Affordable and affordability are its two most useful derivatives.
normal.cn: affordable 与 affordability 是它最有用的两个派生词。

normal.en: The a- in afford is not the Latin prefix ad-, which is a common trap.
normal.cn: afford 里的 a- 并不是拉丁前缀 ad-，这是常见的误解。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket with just enough slack to hold one more coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个口袋只剩一点点余量，正好还能装下一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that can carry one more truck but not two.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥还能承受一辆卡车，却承受不了两辆。

abstract.en: See time as a purse too: spending a week is spending money you cannot earn back.
abstract.cn: 把时间也看成一个钱包：花掉一周，就是花掉挣不回来的钱。

examples.en: They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
examples.cn: 那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。

examples.en: The job afforded her a chance to work abroad.
examples.cn: 这份工作给了她一个到国外工作的机会。

examples.en: The bill arrived at the end of a long month.
examples.cn: 账单在漫长的一个月结束时到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福德」——阿（a）福（fu）德（de），有福有德、手头宽裕，就负担得起。

root: 古英语 geforthian「推进、完成」来自 forth「向前」，中古英语弱化为 aforthen，后固定为 afford；开头的 a- 并非拉丁前缀 ad-。

sensesIntro.en: One budget image runs through the word: money, time, opportunity, and risk are all things you may or may not be able to carry.
sensesIntro.cn: 整条义项线贯穿着同一个「预算」意象：钱、时间、机会与风险，都是你可能承担得起也可能承担不起的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket with enough slack for one more thing
core.cn: 核心意象：一个还装得下一样东西的口袋

branches.en: Money enough to pay the price.
branches.cn: 足以支付价格的钱。

branches.en: Time or strength enough to attempt something.
branches.cn: 足以尝试某事的时间或精力。

branches.en: Means that yield something for others.
branches.cn: 能为他人产出些什么的财力。

branches.en: Capacity to carry a bad outcome.
branches.cn: 承受坏结果的能力。

branches.en: Paying a bill and paying for a mistake.
branches.cn: 付账单与为错误付代价。

intro.en: Afford is native English, so its construction is mainly prefixes and suffixes added to a Germanic core rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本族词，其构词主要是日耳曼语核心加前后缀，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the -able in affordable, however, is a Latin suffix that reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；不过 affordable 里的 -able 是经法语进入英语的拉丁语后缀。

items.meaning: be able to do without ruin

definition_zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外；在战场上
definition_en: at a distance from home or from the usual place, especially in far afield; in older use, out in open country or on campaign
core_image: 离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去
scene: 这家小厂原本只卖给邻镇，如今客户远及海外。The firm now sells far afield.
sceneCN: 这里 afield 是「在远处」（第 1 个义项：远离本地、到远方去）；句意为这家厂如今把货卖到很远的地方。核心画面是离开自家那块地，走到外面的田野去。

pos.zh: 在远处；远离家乡；在野外

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（副词，常与 far 或 further 连用）

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 a- 的名词，义为「田地；场地；领域」
field 加 work 构成，义为「实地考察；田野工作」
out 加 field 构成，义为「外场；外围地带」

senses.title: Far from home or the usual place
senses.definition: at a distance from the place where you live or normally work, especially in the phrase far afield
senses.definitionCN: 离你居住或平常工作的地方有一段距离，尤用于 far afield 这一短语
senses.example: Collectors come from far afield to see the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏爱好者从很远的地方赶来看这批藏品。
senses.why: The prefix a- here means on or in, so afield is literally in the field: once you leave your own plot you are out in open country, which is far from home.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 a- 表示「在……上／中」，所以 afield 字面是「在田地里」：一旦离开自家那块地，你就到了外面的旷野，也就是离家很远的地方。

senses.title: Out on open ground or on campaign
senses.definition: out in the open country, or away on a military campaign, the older literal sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 在外面的旷野中，或出征在外，是该词更古老、更字面的用法
senses.example: The regiment spent a whole summer afield.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团整个夏天都在野外驻扎。
senses.why: This sense keeps the original picture unchanged: soldiers and hunters were literally in the fields, away from the town walls.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项原封不动地保留了最初的画面：士兵与猎人确实身处田野，远离城墙之内。

intro.en: Afield is a phrase worn down into one word: the Old English preposition on plus field, meaning in the field, later fused and extended to mean far from home.
intro.cn: afield 是一个短语磨损成的单词：古英语介词 on 加 field，意为「在田地里」，后来融合并引申为「远离家乡」。

items.en: Old English on meant on or in, and in casual speech it wore down to a single unstressed a-.
items.cn: 古英语 on 意为「在……上／中」，在口语中弱化为一个不重读的 a-。

items.en: Old English feld meant open country or unenclosed land, the ancestor of modern field.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为旷野或未围起的土地，是现代 field 的祖先。

items.en: The phrase on felde meant out in the open, used of grazing animals and of soldiers on campaign.
items.cn: 短语 on felde 意为「在旷野中」，用于放牧的牲畜与出征的士兵。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the two words had fused into afeld, written as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，两个词已融合为 afeld，写成一个副词。

items.en: Modern spelling restored the ie of field, and the adverb settled into far afield and further afield, meaning at a distance.
items.cn: 现代拼写恢复了 field 中的 ie，该副词固定用于 far afield 与 further afield，表示「在远处」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the a- adverbs built from nouns; the near-meaning group lists other ways of saying far away.
note.cn: 形近组保留由名词构成的 a- 类副词；近义组列出其他表示「在远处」的说法。

entries.definition: On or onto the land from the water.
entries.definitionCN: 从水上到岸上。

entries.definition: In or to a foreign country.
entries.definitionCN: 在国外；到国外。

entries.definition: Further forward in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上更靠前。

entries.definition: In the state of sleeping.
entries.definitionCN: 处于睡眠状态。

entries.definition: At or from a great distance.
entries.definitionCN: 在远处；从远处。

entries.definition: At a distance from a place or person.
entries.definitionCN: 离某地或某人有一段距离。

entries.definition: In or to a country across the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 在海外；到海外。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处；到别处。

normalIntro.en: Afield is a-, on, plus field, open land: on the field, and therefore away from home.
normalIntro.cn: afield 就是 a-「在……上」加 field「田野」：在田野上，因此也就是离开家。

normal.en: The a- is the worn-down Old English on, the same a- you see in ashore, abroad and asleep.
normal.cn: 这个 a- 是古英语 on 的弱化形式，与 ashore、abroad、asleep 中的 a- 相同。

normal.en: Afield almost always follows far or further, so learn the pair far afield as one chunk.
normal.cn: afield 几乎总跟在 far 或 further 后面，所以把 far afield 当作一个整块来记。

normal.en: It is an adverb, never an adjective: say travellers from far afield, not afield travellers.
normal.cn: 它是副词，绝不作形容词：说 travellers from far afield，不说 afield travellers。

normal.en: Field means open land, so afield keeps the picture of stepping outside your own fence.
normal.cn: field 意为旷野，所以 afield 保留「走出自家围栏」的画面。

normal.en: Do not confuse afield with the field: the first tells where someone is, the second names the ground.
normal.cn: 别把 afield 与 the field 混淆：前者说人在哪里，后者指那块地。

abstract.en: Picture your own small plot, then the wide open country beyond its fence.
abstract.cn: 想象自家那一小块地，再想象围栏外辽阔的旷野。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier leaving the town gate and sleeping under the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一个士兵走出城门，在天空下露宿。

abstract.en: Think of a letter that travelled three provinces to reach your desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封跨越三个省才到你桌上的信。

examples.en: The magazine draws its writers from far afield.
examples.cn: 这份杂志的作者来自很远的地方。

examples.en: We had to look further afield for a supplier.
examples.cn: 我们不得不去更远的地方找供应商。

examples.en: Students who study afield often return with new ideas.
examples.cn: 到外地求学的学生回来时常带着新想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲尔德」——阿（a）菲（fi）尔（el）德（d）：走出家门那片田野（field），就是到远处、在野外。

root: 古英语介词 on「在……上」加 feld「旷野、未围之地」构成短语 on felde「在田野中」，十四世纪融合为 afeld，现代拼写恢复 field 的 ie，成为副词 afield，并固定用于 far 或 further afield 表示「在远处」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses start from one step outside the fence: the literal one puts you in open country or on campaign, and the extended one simply measures how far that step took you from home.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都从「走出围栏的那一步」出发：字面义把你放在旷野或出征途中，引申义只是衡量这一步把你带得离家有多远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: out of your own field, into the open
core.cn: 核心意象：离开自家那块地，走到外面的旷野

branches.en: Customers arriving from other provinces.
branches.cn: 客户从外省赶来。

branches.en: Searching beyond the usual local sources.
branches.cn: 到平常的本地渠道之外去寻找。

branches.en: Troops camping on open ground.
branches.cn: 部队在旷野扎营。

branches.en: Hunters working the fields all season.
branches.cn: 猎人整个季节都在田野里。

branches.en: Both put the subject outside the home fence.
branches.cn: 两者都把主体放在自家围栏之外。

intro.en: Afield belongs to a small English pattern where the preposition on wears down to a- and turns a noun into an adverb of place or state.
intro.cn: afield 属于英语中一个小构词模式：介词 on 弱化为 a-，把名词变成表示地点或状态的副词。

latinIntro.en: This word is wholly Germanic, so it has no Latin layer; the table below lists the native pieces instead.
latinIntro.cn: 该词完全来自日耳曼语，没有拉丁语层次；下表列出的是本族语构件。

items.meaning: the outer part of the field

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；不敢的；恐怕（礼貌用语）
definition_en: feeling fear or worry about something; unwilling to do something because of fear; used politely to apologize or give bad news
core_image: 心里往后缩的一步，面对可能到来的危险
scene: 深夜的走廊里，孩子听见楼梯间的响动，抓紧了母亲的衣角。The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
sceneCN: 这里 afraid 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项：对某事物感到恐惧）；句意为孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。画面中可辨识：深夜走廊、楼梯间、抓住衣角的孩子。

pos.zh: 害怕的；担心的；不敢的；（礼貌）恐怕

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（表语形容词）

derivatives.zh: 由 un- 加 afraid 构成，义为「不怕的；无所畏惧的」
afraid 的古体变体，义同「害怕的」，多见于早期英语文本

senses.title: Feeling fear of something
senses.definition: feeling fear because of a person, thing, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人、某物或某种情况而感到恐惧
senses.example: The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。
senses.why: The word began as a participle meaning 'frightened', so the feeling is something done to you before it is something you do.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是意为「被吓到」的分词，所以这种感受先是被施加于你，而不是你主动做出的。

senses.title: Worried about someone or something
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 担心某人或某物可能遭遇不好的事
senses.example: She was afraid for her son, who had not called.
senses.exampleCN: 她为没有打电话来的儿子担心。
senses.why: Fear can point forward as worry: the danger is not here yet, but the mind already reaches toward it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以向前延伸为担忧：危险还没到，心却已经伸向它了。

senses.title: Unwilling to act because of fear
senses.definition: unwilling to do something because of fear or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 因为害怕或疑虑而不愿做某事
senses.example: He was afraid to ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他不敢开口求助。
senses.why: When fear stands in front of an action, it becomes a refusal, and afraid to do names that barrier.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧挡在动作前面，它就成了一种拒绝，afraid to do 指的就是这道障碍。

senses.title: Polite regret: I'm afraid
senses.definition: used politely to introduce an apology, a refusal, or unpleasant news
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地引出歉意、拒绝或坏消息
senses.example: I'm afraid the last train has already left.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕末班车已经开走了。
senses.why: The fear sense softened into social caution: the speaker braces for the listener's disappointment.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧义软化为社交上的谨慎：说话者为听者的失望先做一点心理准备。

intro.en: Afraid began as a participle of a verb meaning 'to frighten', not as a word for fear itself.
intro.cn: afraid 起初是动词「使惊恐」的分词，而不是表示恐惧本身的词。

items.en: The prefix ex- 'out' combined with a Germanic word for peace in Vulgar Latin.
items.cn: 前缀 ex-「出」在俗拉丁语中与一个表示「和平」的日耳曼词结合。

items.en: Exfridare meant 'to disturb the peace, to frighten', literally to put someone out of peace.
items.cn: exfridare 意为「扰乱安宁、使惊恐」，字面是「把人从和平中赶出去」。

items.en: Old French esfreer meant 'to frighten, to alarm' and passed into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 esfreer 意为「使惊恐、使惊慌」，传入中古英语。

items.en: The verb affraien meant 'to frighten', and its participle became the adjective afraid.
items.cn: 动词 affraien 意为「使惊恐」，其分词演变为形容词 afraid。

items.en: Afraid settled as a predicate adjective and later took on the polite sense of I'm afraid.
items.cn: afraid 固定为表语形容词，后来又发展出 I'm afraid 的礼貌用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same frighten family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for fear and worry.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「使惊恐」词族；近义组收表示恐惧与忧虑的形容词。

entries.definition: A public fight or disturbance that frightens people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斗殴；扰乱治安」，与 afraid 同出古法语「使惊恐」的动词。

entries.definition: An archaic variant of afraid, meaning frightened.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，afraid 的古体变体，义为「害怕的」，多见于早期文本。

entries.definition: Not frightened; willing to face danger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不怕的；无畏的」，由 un- 加 afraid 构成。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, especially suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受惊的；害怕的」，强调突然被吓到。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, used especially in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」，口语色彩强，常与 of 连用。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, or causing fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」或「可怕的」，比 afraid 更书面。

entries.definition: Worried about something that may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑的；担心的」，对应义项二，但更强调持续不安。

normalIntro.en: Afraid is best remembered as the 'frightened' participle, with the polite phrase I'm afraid as its everyday anchor.
normalIntro.cn: afraid 最好记成「被吓到」的分词，再用 I'm afraid 这个日常说法固定它。

normal.en: The old verb meant to frighten, so afraid is the state of having been frightened.
normal.cn: 古动词意为「使惊恐」，所以 afraid 就是「被吓到」的状态。

normal.en: Be afraid of names the danger, and be afraid to do names the barrier to action.
normal.cn: be afraid of 引出危险对象，be afraid to do 引出行动的障碍。

normal.en: I'm afraid is not about fear at all; it is a polite way to soften bad news.
normal.cn: I'm afraid 与恐惧无关，它是让坏消息变柔和的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Unafraid simply adds un- and reverses the feeling.
normal.cn: unafraid 只是加了 un-，把这种感觉反过来。

normal.en: Affray shares the same frighten source but became a noun for a public disturbance.
normal.cn: affray 共享同一「使惊恐」来源，却变成了表示公共骚乱的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a child stepping back from a dark doorway without knowing why.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从漆黑的门口后退一步，却说不出原因。

abstract.en: Think of fear as a hand on your shoulder pulling you away from the edge.
abstract.cn: 把恐惧想成一只搭在你肩上、把你从边缘拉回的手。

abstract.en: See the polite I'm afraid as a small bow before delivering a disappointment.
abstract.cn: 把礼貌的 I'm afraid 看成送出失望之前的一个小小鞠躬。

examples.en: The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
examples.cn: 孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。

examples.en: I'm afraid we cannot change the booking now.
examples.cn: 恐怕我们现在无法更改预订了。

examples.en: The corridor light flickered twice and went out.
examples.cn: 走廊的灯闪了两下就灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗雷德」——阿（a）弗（fu）雷（lei）德（de），心里一害怕，脚步就往后退。

root: 俗拉丁语 exfridare「扰乱安宁、使惊恐」经古法语 esfreer 进入中古英语动词 affraien，其分词演变为表语形容词 afraid。

sensesIntro.en: From being frightened, the word spreads to worry, to unwillingness, and finally to a polite formula for bad news.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被吓到」出发，这个词扩展到担忧、到不敢行动，最后变成引出坏消息的礼貌套语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken backward from danger
core.cn: 核心意象：面对危险时往后缩的一步

branches.en: Fear with a clear object in front of it.
branches.cn: 面对明确对象时的恐惧。

branches.en: Fear stretched forward into worry.
branches.cn: 恐惧向前延伸为担忧。

branches.en: Fear turned into a refusal to act.
branches.cn: 恐惧转化为拒绝行动。

branches.en: Fear softened into social politeness.
branches.cn: 恐惧软化为社交礼貌。

branches.en: The feeling and the barrier it creates.
branches.cn: 这种感受以及它造成的障碍。

intro.en: Afraid is a fossilized participle, so its building blocks are best seen through related words rather than a clean prefix-plus-root split.
intro.cn: afraid 是凝固的分词，所以它的构词最好通过相关词来看，而不是干净地拆成前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Vulgar Latin and Old French, and its Latin pieces are ex- and a Germanic word for peace.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经由俗拉丁语与古法语而来，其拉丁成分是 ex- 与一个表示「和平」的日耳曼词。

latinEntries.example: Exfridare became esfreer in Old French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exfridare 在古法语中变成 esfreer。

latinEntries.example: Esfreer entered Middle English as affraien.
latinEntries.exampleCN: esfreer 作为 affraien 进入中古英语。

definition_zh: 年龄；年岁；老年；时代；时期；变老；陈化
definition_en: the number of years a person or thing has lived, or a long period in history
core_image: 树干上一圈圈年轮，把流走的时间刻成了可以数出的痕迹
scene: 老木匠抚摸着院里的老榆树，一圈一圈数着树干上的年轮。Each ring on the trunk marked an age of slow growth.
sceneCN: 这里 age 是「年龄、年岁」（第 1 个义项：人或物存在的时间长度）；句意为树干上的每一圈年轮都标记着一段缓慢生长的岁月。图中可辨识物件：老榆树、年轮、木匠的手。

pos.zh: 名词：年龄；年岁；老年；时代；时期
动词：变老；使显老；陈化

derivatives.zh: 由 age 加 -ed 构成，义为「年老的；陈年的」
由 age 加 -less 构成，义为「不显老的；永恒的」
由 age 加 -ing 构成，义为「老化；变老的过程」
由 age 加 -ism 构成，义为「年龄歧视」

senses.title: The number of years lived
senses.definition: the number of years that a person or thing has lived or existed
senses.definitionCN: 人或物已经生存或存在的年数
senses.example: She started learning the piano at the age of six.
senses.exampleCN: 她六岁开始学钢琴。
senses.why: Latin aetas, from aevum 'lifetime', counted the span a person or thing had lived; the noun began as that number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aetas 出自 aevum「一生」，用来计算人或物已活过的跨度；名词最初就是这个数字。

senses.title: The later part of life
senses.definition: the state of being old, or the late period of a person's life
senses.definitionCN: 年老的状态，或一个人生命的晚期
senses.example: His hands showed the marks of age, but his eyes were still bright.
senses.exampleCN: 他的双手留下岁月的痕迹，眼睛却依然明亮。
senses.why: The same span, seen from its end, turns from a count of years into the condition of having many of them.
senses.whyCN: 同一段时间跨度从末端看，就从「年数的计数」转为「年数很多的状态」。

senses.title: A historical period
senses.definition: a particular period of history, often named after its dominant technology or culture
senses.definitionCN: 历史上某个特定时期，常以其主导的技术或文化命名
senses.example: The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age in many parts of the world.
senses.exampleCN: 在世界许多地方，青铜时代紧接石器时代而来。
senses.why: Aetas also named a long stretch of the world's life, so the word widened from one person's years to a whole era.
senses.whyCN: aetas 也指世界存续的一大段时光，于是词义从一个人的年岁扩展到整个时代。

senses.title: A stage in development
senses.definition: a distinct period in the development of something, such as an industry or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 事物发展过程中的一个明显阶段，如某个行业或某种观念
senses.example: The company has entered a new age of digital trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司已进入数字贸易的新时期。
senses.why: Institutions are pictured as living things; if they live, they too pass through ages.
senses.whyCN: 机构被比作有生命的东西；既然有生命，它们也会经历一个个时期。

senses.title: To grow old
senses.definition: to become older, or to show the effects of passing years
senses.definitionCN: 变老，或显出岁月流逝的影响
senses.example: He has aged a great deal since the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他老了很多。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to age is to undergo what the noun measures.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：age 就是经历名词所计量的那件事。

senses.title: To make someone look old
senses.definition: to cause a person to look older than they are, usually through worry or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使人看起来比实际年龄更老，常因忧虑或艰辛所致
senses.example: Years of worry had aged her beyond her years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的忧虑使她显得比实际年龄苍老。
senses.why: The verb takes a causative turn: time does its work on someone, and the speaker names the result.
senses.whyCN: 动词带上使役色彩：时间在某人身上起作用，说话人则点明结果。

senses.title: To mature with time
senses.definition: to be left for a period so that flavor, texture, or quality improves
senses.definitionCN: 放置一段时间，使风味、质地或品质变得更好
senses.example: The cheese is left to age for two years in a cool cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪要在阴凉的地窖里陈化两年。
senses.why: Here time is a craftsman: the object is not merely getting older but being improved by the wait.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间是工匠：对象不只是变旧，而是在等待中被改良。

intro.en: Age goes back through Old French to Latin aetas, a word for a lifetime that also came to name whole eras.
intro.cn: age 经由古法语上溯到拉丁语 aetas，这个词本指一生，后来也用来指整个时代。

items.en: *aiw- is reconstructed as 'vital force, life, long time', the root behind words for age and eternity.
items.cn: 原始印欧语 *aiw- 被重构为「生命力、生命、长久」，是表示年龄与永恒的词根。

items.en: Aevum meant a span of time or a lifetime, and aetas, from the same family, meant age or a stage of life.
items.cn: aevum 意为「一段时间、一生」，同族的 aetas 意为「年岁、人生的阶段」。

items.en: Old French aage, derived from aetas, named both a person's years and a historical period.
items.cn: 古法语 aage 出自 aetas，既指人的年岁，也指历史上的一段时期。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century and kept the personal and the historical senses together.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，人的年岁与历史时期两种含义一并保留。

items.en: The verb grew out of the noun, and compounds such as middle-aged and teenage spread the idea of a measured span.
items.cn: 动词用法由名词生长出来，middle-aged、teenage 等复合词把「可度量的时间跨度」这一观念扩散开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same root; the near-meaning group gathers time words of different length.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示不同长度时间的词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone or something that is old or has been left to mature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年老的；陈化的」，指人或物年纪大或经过陈放。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning never seeming to grow old or never ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不显老的；永恒的」，指似乎不会变老或没有终点。

entries.definition: The noun or adjective for the process of growing older.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「老化；变老的」，指逐渐年长的过程。

entries.definition: A long and distinct period of history named for its character or events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时代；纪元」，指以特征或事件命名的漫长历史时期。

entries.definition: A period marked by a memorable event or a new stage of development.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「纪元；新时代」，指以重大事件或新发展阶段为标志的时期。

entries.definition: A length of time defined by particular features or events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时期；阶段」，指具有特定特征或事件的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to rings, candles and the look of the letters.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与年轮、蜡烛以及字母外形联系起来。

normal.en: Think of tree rings: one ring for each year of age.
normal.cn: 想到树的年轮：每长一岁就多一圈。

normal.en: Picture a birthday cake with candles, one for every year of age.
normal.cn: 想象插着蜡烛的生日蛋糕，每一根代表一岁。

normal.en: AGE begins with the same letters as 'A Great Era'.
normal.cn: age 的开头字母可以读成「A Great Era」，暗示一段伟大的时期。

normal.en: Link age with aged: both describe what long years do to a person.
normal.cn: 把 age 与 aged 连在一起记：两者都描述漫长岁月在人身上留下的痕迹。

normal.en: The word hides 'a generation': age is a generation measured in years.
normal.cn: 这个词里藏着「a generation」的影子：年龄就是以年为单位量出的一代时光。

abstract.en: Age is time made visible: rings, wrinkles and dates all count it.
abstract.cn: 年龄是看得见的时间：年轮、皱纹与日期都在为它计数。

abstract.en: From one life span the word stretches out to whole civilizations.
abstract.cn: 从一个生命的长度出发，这个词延伸到了整个文明。

abstract.en: To age is to let time do its slow work, whether on a body or on cheese.
abstract.cn: 变老就是让时间慢慢做功，无论作用在身体还是在奶酪上。

examples.en: At the age of thirty, she changed careers completely.
examples.cn: 三十岁时，她彻底换了行业。

examples.en: He has aged gracefully, still walking five kilometers every morning.
examples.cn: 他老得很从容，每天早晨仍走五公里。

examples.en: The wine needs time to age before it is bottled.
examples.cn: 这酒在装瓶前需要时间陈化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶，这」：诶，这老人多大岁数了？说的就是年龄。

root: 拉丁语 aetas（年岁、一生）与 aevum（漫长的时间）同源，原始印欧语 *aiw- 表示「生命力、长久」，由「一生的长度」引申出「年龄」与「时代」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from a counted life span, then widens to historical periods and to the process of growing or maturing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从可计数的一生长度出发，进而扩展到历史时期，以及变老、陈化的过程。

core.en: THE SPAN OF LIVED TIME
core.cn: 生命走过的长度

branches.en: the measured length of life
branches.cn: 量出的一生长度

branches.en: the late part of that span
branches.cn: 这段长度的末端

branches.en: a span widened to history or to a stage
branches.cn: 扩展到历史或发展阶段的跨度

branches.en: time working on a body
branches.cn: 时间作用于身体

branches.en: time working for quality
branches.cn: 时间作用于品质

intro.en: Age is a free-standing word, but it joins freely with suffixes and with other nouns to name people and periods.
intro.cn: age 是独立成词的词，但它能自由地接后缀、也能与其他名词组合，用来指人和时期。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin family gathers around aevum and aetas, the words for a lifetime and for an era.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词族围绕 aevum 与 aetas，也就是表示「一生」与「时代」的两个词。

items.meaning: having lived many years, or having been left to mature
items.example: The aged farmer still works in the fields.
items.exampleCN: 年迈的农夫仍在田里劳作。

items.meaning: never seeming to grow old, or never coming to an end
items.example: Her face seemed ageless in the soft light.
items.exampleCN: 柔和的光线下，她的面容似乎永不衰老。

items.example: Aging is a natural part of every life.
items.exampleCN: 变老是一切生命自然的一部分。

items.meaning: unfair treatment of people because of their age
items.example: Ageism can cost experienced workers their jobs.
items.exampleCN: 年龄歧视可能让经验丰富的工人失去工作。

items.example: The middle-aged man took up running last spring.
items.exampleCN: 那位中年男子去年春天开始跑步。

items.meaning: relating to people from thirteen to nineteen years old
items.example: She writes novels for teenage readers.
items.exampleCN: 她为青少年读者写小说。

items.meaning: existing for a very long time
items.example: The two villages settled an age-old dispute at last.
items.exampleCN: 两个村子终于解决了由来已久的争端。

items.meaning: younger than the age required by law
items.meaningCN: 未成年的；未达法定年龄的
items.example: The club refuses entry to underage visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部拒绝未达年龄的来客入内。

items.meaning: older than the age allowed for a purpose
items.example: The team had to drop its overage players.
items.exampleCN: 球队不得不放弃超龄球员。

latinEntries.meaning: a lifetime, a long span of time, eternity

latinEntries.structure: from aevum, with the -t- noun suffix
latinEntries.meaning: age, a stage of life, a period of history
latinEntries.meaningCN: 年岁；人生阶段；历史时期

definition_zh: 代理机构；经销处；（政府）机构；代理关系；能动性；作用
definition_en: a business or organization that acts for others, or the power to act and produce effects
core_image: 把事务交到一只可靠的手里，让它替你出面办理
scene: 旅行社的柜台前排着长队，工作人员正替客人预订远行的机票。The travel agency handled every booking, visa and hotel for the group.
sceneCN: 这里 agency 是「代理机构」（第 1 个义项：代他人办理事务的商业机构）；句意为这家旅行社替整个团队办妥了订票、签证与酒店。图中可辨识物件：柜台、机票、行李箱。

pos.zh: 名词：代理机构；经销处；政府机构；能动性

collocations.zh: 通过……的作用；经由……的中介

derivatives.zh: 由 ag- 加 -ent 构成，义为「代理人；行为者」
由 agent 加 -ial 构成，义为「代理的；行为者的」
由 sub- 加 agency 构成，义为「分代理处；支机构」

senses.title: A business that acts for clients
senses.definition: a company that provides a service by acting on behalf of its clients, such as a travel or advertising agency
senses.definitionCN: 代客户办理事务以提供服务的公司，如旅行社或广告公司
senses.example: The travel agency booked our flights and hotels.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅行社替我们订好了机票和酒店。
senses.why: Latin agere meant to do; an agency is a business whose whole work is doing things for other people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做」；代理机构就是一家专门替别人办事的公司。

senses.title: A public body of the state
senses.definition: an official organization, usually part of a government, that administers a public service or regulation
senses.definitionCN: 通常隶属于政府的官方机构，负责管理某项公共服务或规章
senses.example: A government agency is investigating the river pollution.
senses.exampleCN: 一个政府机构正在调查这条河的污染。
senses.why: The state acts through bodies of its own; each such body is the state's agent, hence its agency.
senses.whyCN: 国家通过自身的机构行事；每个机构都是国家的代理人，所以称为 agency。

senses.title: The relation of acting for another
senses.definition: the legal relationship in which one person is authorized to act on behalf of another
senses.definitionCN: 一方获授权代表另一方行事的法律关系
senses.example: The agency agreement allows him to sign contracts for the company.
senses.exampleCN: 这份代理协议允许他代表公司签署合同。
senses.why: Here the word names not the office but the tie itself: the authority to do another's business.
senses.whyCN: 这里指的不是机构，而是关系本身：替他人办事的那份授权。

senses.title: The capacity to act
senses.titleCN: 能动性；自主行动的能力
senses.definition: the inner power of a person or group to act independently and make choices
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体独立行动、作出选择的内在力量
senses.example: Children need room to develop their own agency.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子需要空间来发展自己的能动性。
senses.why: From an office full of agents the word abstracted the bare power of acting, a sense central to social science.
senses.whyCN: 从满是代理人的机构出发，这个词抽象出了纯粹的「行动能力」，这是社会科学的核心概念。

senses.title: The force that brings about an effect
senses.definition: the means or influence through which something is done or an effect is produced
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事或产生某种效果所凭借的手段或影响
senses.example: The reform succeeded through the agency of a few determined teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这场改革借助几位坚定教师的力量取得了成功。
senses.why: If an agent is what does a thing, then agency can also mean the working of that force.
senses.whyCN: 既然 agent 是做事的那一方，agency 也就可以指那股力量的作用。

senses.title: A local branch of a service
senses.definition: a local office or branch through which a larger organization serves a district
senses.definitionCN: 较大的机构在某一地区设立、用来服务当地的办事处
senses.example: The bank opened a small agency in the mountain town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在山中小镇开设了一个代理处。
senses.why: A branch is the parent organization acting at a distance, a piece of the agency placed in one place.
senses.whyCN: 分支机构就是母机构在远处的行动，是代理机构安放在某一处的一块。

intro.en: Agency comes from the Latin verb 'to do', through the noun for an agent's office.
intro.cn: agency 出自拉丁语表示「做」的动词，经由表示「代理人事务」的名词而来。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion; its present participle agens named the one who acts.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」；其现在分词 agens 指「行动的人」。

items.en: Agentia named the office or function of an agent, the business of doing something for another.
items.cn: agentia 指代理人的职务或职能，即替他人办事这件事。

items.en: Old French agence carried the commercial sense of an office that acts for clients.
items.cn: 古法语 agence 带有「替客户办事的机构」这一商业含义。

items.en: English adopted agency for a place or person acting on behalf of another, first in trade and law.
items.cn: 英语借入 agency，用来指代他人行事的地方或人，最早见于商业与法律。

items.en: Political and social writing added the abstract sense of capacity to act, now familiar as human agency.
items.cn: 政治与社会学写作又增添了「行动能力」这一抽象义，如今常见于「人的能动性」这一说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same acting root; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of organizations.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「行动」词根的一族词；近义组收不同类型的组织。

entries.definition: A person who acts for another, especially in business or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人；经纪人」，指替他人行事的人，尤见于商业或法律。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to the power of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理的；与行动能力有关的」。

entries.definition: A list of things to be done or discussed at a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「议程；待办事项」，与 agency 词形相近但来源不同。

entries.definition: An office or department, often a government one, that handles a particular service.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「局；办事处」，常指负责某项服务的政府机构。

entries.definition: A business company, especially one providing professional services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司；事务所」，尤指提供专业服务的商号。

entries.definition: An established organization such as a bank, school, or hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构；制度」，指银行、学校、医院等已设立的组织。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to agents, travel desks and the ending that names an office.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与代理人、旅行社柜台以及表示机构的词尾联系起来。

normal.en: AGENCY contains agent: an agency is where agents work.
normal.cn: agency 里面藏着 agent：代理机构就是代理人工作的地方。

normal.en: Think of a travel agency that acts for you when you cannot go yourself.
normal.cn: 想想旅行社：你自己去不了时，它替你跑腿。

normal.en: The ending -cy turns agent into the place or business of agents.
normal.cn: 词尾 -cy 把 agent 变成代理人所在的场所或买卖。

normal.en: Break it into a-gen-cy and hear 'an agent sees to it'.
normal.cn: 拆成 a-gen-cy，听起来像「an agent sees to it」，即一位代理人在照看这件事。

normal.en: A government agency is a public body that acts for the state.
normal.cn: 政府机构就是代国家行事的公共部门。

abstract.en: Agency is action that has been handed to someone trusted.
abstract.cn: 代理就是把行动交到可信的人手里。

abstract.en: The word moves from a building full of agents to the bare power to act.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一屋子代理人，走到赤裸裸的行动能力。

abstract.en: When people speak of human agency, they mean the will to change things.
abstract.cn: 人们谈人的能动性时，说的是改变事物的意志。

examples.en: The travel agency arranged everything, from visas to airport pickup.
examples.cn: 旅行社把一切安排妥当，从签证到接机。

examples.en: She felt she had no agency in the decision that changed her life.
examples.cn: 在那项改变她人生的决定里，她觉得自己毫无主动权。

examples.en: Through the agency of a mutual friend, the two rivals finally met.
examples.cn: 在一位共同朋友的中介下，两位对手终于见了面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶，真细」：诶，真细致，代理机构把每件事都替你办妥了。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的现在分词 agens 指「做事的人」，加 -tia 构成 agentia「代理的事务」，再经古法语 agence 进入英语，核心是「替他人行事」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a business that acts for clients, spreads to public bodies and legal ties, and ends with abstract power and local branches.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从替客户办事的商业机构开始，扩展到政府机构与法律关系，最后落在抽象的行动能力与地方分支上。

core.en: THE POWER TO ACT FOR ANOTHER

intro.en: Agency belongs to the large family of ag- words, all built on the Latin verb for doing and driving.
intro.cn: agency 属于庞大的 ag- 词族，这一族都建立在拉丁语表示「做与驱动」的动词上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base ag- produces agent, agenda, act and agile, each naming a different face of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 ag- 生出 agent、agenda、act、agile，各自呈现行动的一个侧面。

items.meaning: one who acts, or one who acts for another
items.example: The agent signed the contract for the singer.
items.exampleCN: 代理人替这位歌手签了合同。

items.meaning: relating to an agent or to agency
items.meaningCN: 代理的；与行动者有关的

items.meaning: a secondary agent who works under another

items.exampleCN: 每位副代理人都向主代理人汇报。

items.meaning: a branch agency under a larger one

items.exampleCN: 这家保险公司在该县开设了一个分代理处。

items.example: The agency-wide review begins next month.
items.exampleCN: 全机构范围的审查下个月开始。

items.meaning: naming the doer of an action

items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 在 teacher 中表示施动者。

items.meaning: someone free to act or sign independently
items.example: After the season, he became a free agent.
items.exampleCN: 赛季结束后，他成了自由球员。

items.meaning: a publicist who handles publicity for a client

items.meaning: a business that arranges trips for clients
items.example: The travel agency found us a cheap flight.
items.exampleCN: 旅行社替我们找到了一班便宜航班。

definition_zh: 议程；待办事项清单；政治议题；隐秘意图
definition_en: a list of matters to be discussed or done, especially at a meeting
core_image: 一张写满待办事项的清单，摆在会议桌的最前面
scene: 会议开始前，秘书把印好的清单放在每位参会者面前。The first item on the agenda was the city budget.
sceneCN: 这里 agenda 是「议程」（第 1 个义项：会议要讨论事项的清单）；句意为议程上的第一项是城市预算。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、打印清单、文件夹。

pos.zh: 名词：议程；待办事项；政治议题

derivatives.zh: agenda 的拉丁语单数形式，义为「单件待办事项」
由 agenda 加 setting 构成的复合词，义为「议程设置」

senses.title: A list for a meeting
senses.definition: a list of the items to be discussed at a meeting, usually in a fixed order
senses.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单，通常按固定顺序排列
senses.example: The first item on the agenda was the city budget.
senses.exampleCN: 议程上的第一项是城市预算。
senses.why: Latin agenda is the neuter plural of the future participle of agere, literally 'things to be done'; a meeting list is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agenda 是 agere 将来分词的中性复数，字面就是「该做的事」；会议清单正是这个意思。

senses.title: A personal list of tasks
senses.definition: a private list of things that a person intends to do, often kept as a reminder
senses.definitionCN: 个人打算完成的事项清单，常留作提醒
senses.example: He kept a short agenda of tasks beside his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桌旁放着一张简短的待办清单。
senses.why: The 'things to be done' need not belong to a meeting; anyone can write down what must be done next.
senses.whyCN: 「该做的事」不必属于会议；任何人都可以写下接下来必须做的事。

senses.title: The issues a group pushes
senses.definition: the set of issues that a government, party, or organization treats as important
senses.definitionCN: 政府、政党或组织视为重要的议题集合
senses.example: Climate change is now high on the political agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化如今在政治议题中占据重要位置。
senses.why: A political body also works from a list of what it means to do; that list becomes its public agenda.
senses.whyCN: 政治团体同样按一份「打算做什么」的清单行事；这份清单就成了它公开的议程。

senses.title: A concealed intention
senses.titleCN: 隐秘意图；不可告人的目的
senses.definition: a hidden motive or plan behind an action that appears innocent
senses.definitionCN: 表面无害的行为背后隐藏的动机或计划
senses.example: The committee suspected a hidden agenda behind the generous offer.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会怀疑这份慷慨提议背后另有隐秘意图。
senses.why: If there is an open agenda, there can be a hidden one: a list of things to be done that is kept out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 既然有公开的议程，就可能有隐藏的议程：一份不让人看见的待办清单。

senses.title: A programme of action
senses.definition: a planned programme of measures that an organization intends to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 某组织打算实施的一整套措施计划
senses.example: The party published its agenda for reform in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在春天公布了改革纲领。
senses.why: The list of things to be done grows into a full programme when the doer is a large organization.
senses.whyCN: 当行动者是庞大的组织时，这份待办清单就会长成一套完整的纲领。

senses.title: The printed meeting document
senses.definition: the printed booklet or sheet that lists the order of business for a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 列出会议事务顺序的印刷册页或单页
senses.example: Delegates received the agenda two days before the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们在峰会前两天收到了议程册。
senses.why: Here the abstract list takes physical form: the paper that participants hold in their hands.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象的清单有了实体形态：参会者手里拿着的那张纸。

intro.en: Agenda is Latin for 'things to be done', a plural participle that English borrowed whole.
intro.cn: agenda 是拉丁语「该做的事」，一个复数分词形式被英语整体借入。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion, the source of a large family of action words.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，是一大批行动类词语的源头。

items.en: Agenda is the neuter plural of the future passive participle, so it means 'the things that must be done'.
items.cn: agenda 是将来被动分词的中性复数，因此意为「必须被做的事」。

items.en: The word was used for the list of items in a church service, an early written agenda.
items.cn: 这个词曾用于指教堂礼拜程序清单，是较早的成文议程。

items.en: English borrowed agenda as a list of matters to be attended to, first in religious and official use.
items.cn: 英语借入 agenda，指需要处理的事项清单，最早用于宗教与公务场合。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word widened to the political programme a group intends to carry out.
items.cn: 二十世纪时，词义扩展到某团体打算推行的政治纲领。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same doing root; the near-meaning group gathers lists and plans of events.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「做」词根的一族词；近义组收各种清单与日程安排。

entries.definition: A person who acts for another, especially in business or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人」，指替他人行事的人，尤见于商业或法律。

entries.definition: A business or organization that acts on behalf of others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构」，指代他人行事的商业或公共组织。

entries.definition: The rare singular of agenda, meaning a single item to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，agenda 的罕见单数形式，义为「单件待办事项」。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times at which events are to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日程表；时间表」，列出事件发生的时间。

entries.definition: A chart showing the times of classes, trains, or other events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时刻表；课程表」，标出课程、列车等的时间。

entries.definition: A planned series of events or actions with a stated purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「计划；节目单」，指有既定目的一系列活动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to meeting lists, Latin participles and the idea of things still to be done.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与会议清单、拉丁语分词以及「还没做的事」这一观念联系起来。

normal.en: AGENDA sounds like 'a gen da': a general list for the day.
normal.cn: agenda 读起来像「a gen da」，可以想成一天的总清单。

normal.en: Picture the printed list placed in front of every chair at a meeting.
normal.cn: 想象会议中每把椅子前都摆着一份打印清单。

normal.en: Agenda and agent share the same start: both are about doing things.
normal.cn: agenda 与 agent 开头相同：两者都与「做事」有关。

normal.en: The word literally means 'things to be done', so it always points forward.
normal.cn: 这个词字面就是「该做的事」，所以永远指向未来。

normal.en: Remember 'hidden agenda': a list kept in a pocket instead of on the table.
normal.cn: 记住 hidden agenda 这个说法：一份藏在口袋里而不是摆在桌上的清单。

abstract.en: An agenda is a promise about what will be done next.
abstract.cn: 议程就是关于接下来要做什么的一份承诺。

abstract.en: Whoever writes the list decides what the group will notice.
abstract.cn: 写清单的人，决定了这个群体将注意到什么。

abstract.en: A hidden agenda is a plan wearing the mask of an innocent request.
abstract.cn: 隐秘议程就是戴着无害请求面具的计划。

examples.en: The chair asked whether anyone wished to add an item to the agenda.
examples.cn: 主席询问是否有人想在议程上增加一项。

examples.en: Affordable housing is at the top of the mayor's agenda.
examples.cn: 可负担住房是市长议程上的首要事项。

examples.en: They agreed to meet, but each side brought its own agenda.
examples.cn: 他们同意会面，但双方各怀自己的盘算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额，真大」：额，这份议程真大，条目一页接一页。

root: 拉丁语 agere（做、驱动）的将来被动分词中性复数 agenda，字面为「必须被做的事」，英语整体借入后固定为「议程」。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from a literal list of things to be done, through meeting lists and political priorities, to concealed intentions.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从字面的「待办之事」出发，经过会议清单与政治优先事项，最后落到隐藏的意图。

items.example: The agent closed the deal quickly.
items.exampleCN: 代理人很快谈成了这笔交易。

items.meaning: the office or business of an agent
items.example: The agency hired two new translators.
items.exampleCN: 这家代理机构聘用了两名新译员。

items.meaning: a single item to be done
items.example: Each agendum was debated for ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 每一项待办事项都辩论了十分钟。

items.meaning: the power to decide what others discuss
items.meaningCN: 议程设置；决定他人讨论内容的权力
items.example: The report studied agenda-setting in local media.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告研究了地方媒体的议程设置。

items.meaning: one point on a meeting list
items.example: Budget reform was the last agenda item.
items.exampleCN: 预算改革是最后一项议程。

items.meaning: able to move or think quickly
items.example: The agile team changed plans overnight.
items.exampleCN: 这个灵活的团队一夜之间改了计划。

items.meaning: the quality of being quick and nimble
items.example: Her agility surprised the older players.
items.exampleCN: 她的敏捷让年长的球员吃了一惊。

items.meaning: to shake, stir up, or campaign actively
