definition_zh: 代理人；经纪人；特工；动因；剂；施事者
definition_en: a person who acts for another, or a thing that produces an effect
core_image: 被派出去替主人办事的那双手
scene: 谈判室里，一位受雇的中间人替双方传递条件。The agent negotiated the deal on behalf of the singer.
sceneCN: 这里 agent 是「代理人」（第 1 个义项：受雇代他人办事的人）；句意为这位代理人代表歌手谈成了这笔交易。图中可辨识物件：谈判桌、合同、录音笔。

pos.zh: 名词：代理人；经纪人；特工；动因；剂

derivatives.zh: 由 agent 加 -cy 构成，义为「代理机构；代理业务」
由 agent 加 -ial 构成，义为「代理的；行为者的」
由 agent 加 -ive 构成，义为「施事的；表示施动者的」
由 sub- 加 agent 构成，义为「副代理人；分代理人」

senses.title: One who acts for another
senses.definition: a person who is employed to act on behalf of another person or company
senses.definitionCN: 受雇代表他人或公司行事的人
senses.example: The agent negotiated the deal on behalf of the singer.
senses.exampleCN: 这名代理人代表歌手谈成了这笔交易。
senses.why: Latin agens is 'the one doing'; an agent is simply the person who does the business that someone else cannot do in person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agens 就是「正在做事的人」；代理人不过是替别人去做那件本人无法亲自办的事。

senses.title: A secret operative
senses.definition: a person secretly employed by a government to gather information or carry out operations
senses.definitionCN: 受政府秘密雇用、负责搜集情报或执行任务的人
senses.example: The agent passed the files to headquarters at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这名特工在午夜把文件交给了总部。
senses.why: A spy is also someone acting for another power, but in secret; the neutral word hides the secrecy.
senses.whyCN: 间谍同样是替另一股势力行事的人，只是行事隐秘；这个中性词把秘密藏了起来。

senses.title: A cause of change
senses.definition: a person or force that brings about change or produces an effect
senses.definitionCN: 带来变化或产生效果的人或力量
senses.example: She was the agent of change in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那家老厂里变革的推动者。
senses.why: If an agent does things, it can also be the doer behind an event, not only a hired representative.
senses.whyCN: 既然 agent 是做事的一方，它也可以指事件背后的推动者，而不只是受雇的代表。

senses.title: An active substance
senses.definition: a substance that produces a particular effect, especially in chemistry or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 产生特定效果的物质，尤用于化学或医学
senses.example: Soap is a cleansing agent that lifts grease from cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 肥皂是一种去污剂，能把油污从布上带走。
senses.why: Science extended the word from people to things: whatever produces an effect is treated as the doer.
senses.whyCN: 科学把这个词从人扩展到物：凡是能产生效果的，都被当成施动者。

senses.title: The doer in a sentence
senses.definition: the person or thing that performs the action of a verb in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 句子中执行动词所表示动作的人或物
senses.example: In the sentence, the dog is the agent of the biting.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，狗是咬这个动作的施事者。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the role of the doer, the participant that carries out the action.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借用了这个词来表示「执行者」的角色，即承担动作的那个成分。

senses.title: A local representative
senses.definition: a business or person that represents a company in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区代表某公司的商号或个人
senses.example: Our agent in Shanghai handles all orders from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在上海的代理商处理东部地区的全部订单。
senses.why: An organization cannot be everywhere at once, so it places an agent wherever it needs a hand.
senses.whyCN: 组织无法同时出现在所有地方，于是它把代理人安放在需要人手的地方。

intro.en: Agent is the Latin participle for 'one who is doing', carried into English through French.
intro.cn: agent 是拉丁语中表示「正在做事的人」的分词，经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or set in motion; it is the verb behind act, agenda and agile as well.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、使运动」，act、agenda、agile 等词也出自它。

items.en: The present participle agens, stem agent-, named the person in the middle of doing something.
items.cn: 现在分词 agens 的词干是 agent-，指正在做事的那个人。

items.en: Old French agent kept the sense of a person who acts, especially in legal and commercial matters.
items.cn: 古法语 agent 保留了「行事之人」的含义，尤用于法律与商业事务。

items.en: English adopted agent first for a deputy or representative, then for any active cause.
items.cn: 英语先把它用作「代表、副手」，随后扩展到任何起作用的动因。

items.en: Chemistry and grammar added the agent as a substance or the doer of a verb, widening the word far beyond people.
items.cn: 化学与语法又让 agent 分别指药剂和动词的执行者，使这个词远远超出人的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns and adjectives; the near-meaning group gathers people who act for others.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词与形容词；近义组收替他人行事的人。

entries.definition: A business or organization that acts on behalf of others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构」，指代他人行事的商业或公共组织。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to the power of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理的；与行动能力有关的」。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a form that names the doer of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「施事的」，用于说明某个形式表示动作的执行者。

entries.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表」，指被选出替群体发言或行事的人。

entries.definition: A person who buys and sells goods or services for others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经纪人」，指替他人买卖货物或服务的人。

entries.definition: A person sent to represent others at a meeting or event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表；使节」，指被派去代表他人出席会议或活动的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to deputised work, spies and the '-ent' ending that marks a person.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与受托办事、特工以及表示「人」的词尾 -ent 联系起来。

normal.en: AGENT ends in -ent, the ending found in 'student' and 'resident': a person.
normal.cn: agent 以 -ent 结尾，student 与 resident 也用这个结尾，提示它指一个人。

normal.en: Picture an actor's agent: someone who does the talking so the actor can work.
normal.cn: 想象艺人的经纪人：他负责交涉，艺人才能专心工作。

normal.en: A travel agent acts for you; an agency is where such agents sit.
normal.cn: 旅行代理人替你办事；代理机构就是这些人办公的地方。

normal.en: Secret agent: the word stays neutral while the job stays hidden.
normal.cn: secret agent 这个说法里，词本身中性，工作却隐秘。

normal.en: Agent and agenda start alike because both come from the verb 'to do'.
normal.cn: agent 与 agenda 开头相同，因为两者都出自表示「做」的那个动词。

abstract.en: An agent is will carried out by another pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 代理人就是由另一双手去执行的意志。

abstract.en: The word slides easily from people to chemicals and to grammar.
abstract.cn: 这个词轻易地从人滑向化学药剂，再滑向语法。

abstract.en: Every agent stands in a gap where the principal cannot be present.
abstract.cn: 每一个代理人都站在委托人无法亲自到场的那道缝隙里。

examples.en: The agent showed us three houses before we chose one.
examples.cn: 经纪人带我们看了三套房子，我们才作出选择。

examples.en: A secret agent delivered the documents before dawn.
examples.cn: 一名特工在天亮前送出了文件。

examples.en: She acted as her sister's agent during the negotiations.

definition_en: to make a problem, illness, or situation worse, or to annoy someone
core_image: 往已经沉重的担子上再压一块石头
scene: 病人的伤口还没愈合，他又执意下地干活。Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 aggravate 是「使恶化」（第 1 个义项：使问题或病情变得更严重）；句意为缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。图中可辨识物件：绷带、拐杖、病床。

senses.title: To make a condition worse
senses.definition: to make an illness, injury, or bad situation more serious
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤势或糟糕的局面变得更加严重
senses.example: Lack of rest aggravated the injury in his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少休息使他的膝伤更加严重。
senses.why: Latin gravis meant heavy; adding ad- 'toward' made aggravare 'to add weight', so the word pictures a load made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gravis 意为「沉重」；加上 ad-「朝向」构成 aggravare「加重」，词的画面就是一担更沉的负荷。

senses.title: To add to a burden
senses.definition: to increase the weight of a burden, cost, or difficulty that already exists
senses.definitionCN: 增加原有负担、成本或困难的分量
senses.example: The new tax aggravated the burden on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新税加重了小店铺的负担。
senses.why: The same image works for money and work: whatever is already heavy can be made heavier.
senses.whyCN: 同样的画面也适用于金钱与工作：本来沉重的东西还能再被压重。

senses.title: To provoke or annoy
senses.definition: to make someone angry or irritated, especially by repeated behavior
senses.definitionCN: 使人生气或烦躁，尤因反复出现的行为
senses.example: His endless questions aggravated the tired teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了的问题让疲惫的老师很恼火。
senses.why: An added weight is also felt on the nerves; the word shifted from burdens on the body to burdens on the temper.
senses.whyCN: 加在身上的重量也会压在神经上；词义于是从身体的负担转到脾气的负担。

senses.title: To make a legal offence graver
senses.definition: to make an offence more serious in law, usually by an added circumstance such as a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上使罪行更严重，通常因使用武器等附加情节
senses.example: The theft was aggravated by the use of a weapon.
senses.exampleCN: 由于使用了武器，这起盗窃案被认定为加重情节。
senses.why: Law keeps the literal sense: one fact adds weight to another, and the scale of guilt goes up.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了字面义：一个事实给另一个事实增加重量，罪责的天平随之上升。

senses.title: To intensify a conflict
senses.definition: to make hostility or tension between people or groups stronger
senses.definitionCN: 使人与人、群体与群体之间的敌意或紧张变得更强
senses.example: The speech aggravated the tension between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲加剧了两个群体之间的紧张关系。
senses.why: Tension is another kind of load; words can add to it just as weight adds to a cart.
senses.whyCN: 紧张也是一种负荷；言语能像重量压在车上那样，给它再加一层。

senses.title: To make pain sharper
senses.definition: to increase physical pain, especially by movement or pressure on a hurt part
senses.definitionCN: 使身体的疼痛更强，尤因活动或压迫受伤部位
senses.example: Walking up the stairs aggravated the pain in her back.
senses.exampleCN: 上楼梯使她背部的疼痛加剧了。
senses.why: Pain is the most bodily of burdens; anything that presses on it literally adds weight.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛是最身体化的负担；任何压上去的动作都在字面上增加重量。

intro.en: Aggravate is literally 'to add weight', built in Latin from ad- and gravis.
intro.cn: aggravate 字面就是「增加重量」，由拉丁语的 ad- 与 gravis 构成。

items.en: Gravis meant heavy, weighty, or serious, and it also gave English grave, gravity and grief.
items.cn: gravis 意为「沉重的、有分量的、严重的」，也生出英语的 grave、gravity 与 grief。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus gravare 'to weigh down' produced aggravare, to add weight or make heavier.
items.cn: ad-「向」加上 gravare「压重」构成 aggravare，意为「加重、使更沉」。

items.en: The past participle aggravated described something made heavier or more serious.
items.cn: 过去分词 aggravatus 描述被加重、变得更严重的事物。

items.en: English borrowed the word for making a disease or burden worse, the sense that still dominates.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用来指使疾病或负担加重，这一含义至今占主导。

items.en: A colloquial sense 'to annoy' appeared later and is often criticised, though it is now widespread.
items.cn: 「使恼火」这一口语义出现较晚，常被批评，但如今已广泛使用。

note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收表示「使变糟」的动词。

abstract.en: The word keeps the body's scales even when it speaks of feelings.

abstract.en: Many problems grow worse because someone keeps pressing on them.

definition_zh: 好斗的；有攻击性的；侵略的；积极进取的
definition_en: behaving in a hostile or forceful way, or very determined and energetic
core_image: 向前跨出一步，把拳头伸到别人面前
scene: 两位司机在路口争抢车道，一个人先下车大声指责对方。The aggressive driver shouted and stepped toward the other car.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressive 是「好斗的；有攻击性的」（第 1 个义项：以敌对或强硬的方式对待他人）；句意为这名好斗的司机大喊着朝另一辆车走去。图中可辨识物件：路口、两辆汽车、握紧的拳头。

pos.zh: 形容词：好斗的；有攻击性的；侵略的；积极进取的

collocations.zh: 攻击性行为；好斗的举动

derivatives.zh: 由 aggress- 加 -ion 构成，义为「侵略；攻击性行为」
由 aggress- 加 -or 构成，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」
由 aggressive 加 -ly 构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」
由 aggressive 加 -ness 构成，义为「好斗；攻击性」

senses.title: Hostile toward others
senses.definition: behaving in a hostile, forceful, or threatening way toward other people
senses.definitionCN: 以敌对、强硬或威胁的方式对待他人
senses.example: The aggressive driver shouted and stepped toward the other car.
senses.exampleCN: 这名好斗的司机大喊着朝另一辆车走去。
senses.why: Latin gradi meant to step; ad- plus gradi made aggredi 'to step toward', and stepping toward someone with force became aggression.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「迈步」；ad- 加 gradi 构成 aggredi「向……迈步」，带着武力朝人迈步就成了攻击。

senses.title: Invading or warlike
senses.definition: describing a country, army, or act that attacks or seeks to extend power by force
senses.definitionCN: 形容以武力进攻或谋求扩张势力的国家、军队或行为
senses.example: The aggressive army crossed the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这支侵略军在天亮时越过了边界。
senses.why: Nations also step toward one another; when the step crosses a border, the word names outright invasion.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也会互相迈步；当这一步越过边界，这个词就指赤裸裸的侵略。

senses.title: Boldly enterprising
senses.definition: very determined and energetic in pursuing a goal, often used approvingly in business
senses.definitionCN: 为达成目标而极为坚决、精力充沛，在商业中常带赞许意味
senses.example: The firm's aggressive expansion opened ten new stores in a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的激进扩张在一年内开了十家新店。
senses.why: The same forward step can be admired instead of feared: energy pushing toward a target is called aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向前一步，也可以被赞赏而非畏惧：朝目标推进的劲头就被称为积极进取。

senses.title: Forceful in method
senses.definition: applied with great force or pressure, especially in selling, questioning, or negotiating
senses.definitionCN: 以强力或高压方式施行，尤见于推销、提问或谈判
senses.example: Aggressive marketing annoyed many of the older customers.
senses.exampleCN: 强势营销惹恼了不少年长的顾客。
senses.why: A method that pushes its way forward feels like a person stepping into your space, hence the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 一种硬往前推的方法，感觉就像有人踩进你的地盘，于是用同一个形容词。

senses.title: Fast-spreading, as a disease
senses.definition: describing an illness that grows or spreads quickly and is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 形容发展或扩散迅速、难以控制的疾病
senses.example: Doctors found an aggressive form of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生发现这是一种侵袭性很强的疾病。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the image of a force that advances without restraint; a tumour that steps forward fast is aggressive.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「不加约束地推进」的画面；迅速向前推进的肿瘤就被称为侵袭性的。

senses.title: Attacking in sport
senses.definition: playing in an attacking style that seeks to score rather than defend
senses.definitionCN: 采取进攻型打法，力求得分而非防守
senses.example: The team played an aggressive second half and scored twice.
senses.exampleCN: 球队下半场踢得极具攻击性，攻入两球。
senses.why: Sport keeps the literal sense: players step toward the opponent's goal, and the style is named for that advance.
senses.whyCN: 体育保留了字面义：球员朝对方球门迈步，这种打法就以这次推进命名。

intro.en: Aggressive is built from Latin gradi 'to step', with the prefix that means 'toward'.
intro.cn: aggressive 由拉丁语 gradi「迈步」加表示「朝向」的前缀构成。

items.en: Gradi meant to step, walk, or go, and it also gave English grade and gradual.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走、前进」，也生出英语的 grade 与 gradual。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus gradi made aggredi, to step toward something, and often to attack it.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「朝某物迈步」，常引申为攻击。

items.en: The participle aggressus described an approach or an attack already begun.
items.cn: 分词 aggressus 描述已经开始逼近或攻击的状态。

items.en: English formed aggressive from the Latin stem, first meaning inclined to attack.
items.cn: 英语由拉丁词干造出 aggressive，最初意为「倾向攻击的」。

items.en: Business and sport added the approving sense of energetic and determined, so the word now cuts both ways.
items.cn: 商业与体育又添了「精力充沛、坚决」的褒义，于是这个词如今正反两用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root nouns; the near-meaning group gathers words of force and confidence.
note.cn: 形近组收同根名词；近义组收表示强势与自信的词。

entries.definition: The noun for hostile behavior or an act of attack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略；攻击性行为」，指敌对的举动或进攻。

entries.definition: The person or country that starts an attack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」，指发起攻击的人或国家。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a forceful or enterprising manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」，指以强硬或进取的方式。

entries.definition: Openly unfriendly or opposed, like an enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敌对的；怀有敌意的」，像敌人一样公开不友好。

entries.definition: Confident and direct in stating one's views without aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚定自信的」，敢于直接表达观点但不带攻击性。

entries.definition: Strong and effective in expression or action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强有力的」，指表达或行动有力而有效。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to stepping forward, to sales pressure and to a team that keeps attacking.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个记忆钩子把这个词与向前迈步、推销压力以及持续进攻的球队联系起来。

normal.en: AGGREGATE has greg, but AGGRESSIVE has gress: the Latin step.
normal.cn: aggregate 里是 greg，aggressive 里是 gress，后者是拉丁语的「步」。

normal.en: Picture someone stepping toward you with a raised fist.
normal.cn: 想象有人举着拳头朝你迈步而来。

normal.en: An aggressive salesperson follows you down the aisle.
normal.cn: 强势的推销员会一路跟着你走过货架。

normal.en: In business the same word turns into praise: an aggressive plan is a bold plan.
normal.cn: 在商业里同一个词变成褒义：激进计划就是大胆计划。

normal.en: Sport commentators say 'aggressive' when a team keeps pushing forward.
normal.cn: 体育解说员在球队持续前压时会说 aggressive。

abstract.en: Aggression is a step taken across someone else's line.
abstract.cn: 侵犯，就是跨过别人那条线的一步。

abstract.en: The modern word hides its own double edge: drive or threat.
abstract.cn: 这个词把自身的双刃藏了起来：既可以指干劲，也可以指威胁。

abstract.en: A disease can be aggressive because it steps forward faster than treatment.
abstract.cn: 疾病可以很「侵袭」，因为它比治疗推进得更快。

examples.en: The dog became aggressive whenever a stranger approached.
examples.cn: 只要有陌生人靠近，这条狗就变得凶起来。

examples.en: The company adopted an aggressive plan to double its sales.
examples.cn: 公司采取了一项激进计划，要把销售额翻倍。

examples.en: Aggressive questioning made the witness retreat into silence.
examples.cn: 咄咄逼人的提问让证人退入沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「俺哥来势」：俺哥来势汹汹，一副要动手的样子。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ gradi（迈步）构成 aggredi（向……迈步、攻击），其分词 aggressus 进入英语，核心是「带着力度向前逼近」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers hostile people, invading armies, bold business drive, forceful methods, fast-spreading disease and attacking sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖好斗的人、侵略的军队、大胆的商业冲劲、强硬手法、扩散迅速的疾病与进攻型体育。

core.en: STEPPING FORWARD WITH FORCE
core.cn: 带着力度向前逼近

branches.en: a person or army that steps in
branches.cn: 迈步逼近的人或军队

branches.en: the same step admired as drive
branches.cn: 同一步伐被赞为干劲

branches.en: a method that pushes you back
branches.cn: 把你逼退的做法

branches.en: an illness advancing fast
branches.cn: 迅速推进的疾病

branches.en: players stepping toward the goal
branches.cn: 朝球门迈步的球员

intro.en: Aggressive belongs to the grad- family, words of stepping, grading and graduating.
intro.cn: aggressive 属于 grad- 词族，这一族的词都与迈步、分级、毕业有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base grad- means step; prefixes change the direction, and suffixes change the word class.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 grad- 意为「步」；前缀改变方向，后缀改变词性。

items.example: The school has a policy against aggression.
items.exampleCN: 学校有禁止攻击行为的规章。

items.meaning: the one who starts an attack
in a forceful or energetic way
items.example: He argued aggressively for the new plan.
The coach praised the team's aggressiveness.
items.exampleCN: 教练称赞了球队的攻击性。

items.example: They agreed on a nonaggressive approach.
items.exampleCN: 他们商定采取非攻击性的做法。

items.meaningCN: 过于强硬的；过度激进的
items.example: The overaggressive sales pitch scared buyers away.
items.exampleCN: 过度强势的推销把买家吓跑了。
她那种消极对抗的沉默已说明一切。

items.meaning: a step in rank, or a mark of quality
items.example: She moved up a grade last year.

definition_zh: 好斗性；攻击性；（受称赞的）进取劲头
definition_en: the quality of being quick to attack or quarrel; also the bold, forceful drive to win or achieve, praised in sport and business
core_image: 一股向前扑的劲头
scene: 新教练要求球员逼抢更凶，可裁判也盯得更紧。Aggressiveness wins the ball, not the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressiveness 是「进取劲头」（第 2 个义项：主动向前、敢于争取的劲头）；句意为这种劲头能抢到球，却吵不赢架。核心画面是一股向前扑的劲头。

pos.zh: 好斗性；攻击性；进取劲头

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ness 的形容词，义为「好斗的；有进取心的」
aggressive 加 -ly，义为「咄咄逼人地；积极地」
同根名词，义为「侵略；攻击行为」

senses.title: Readiness to attack or quarrel
senses.definition: the quality of being quick to attack, argue or force your way, so that others feel threatened
senses.definitionCN: 动辄攻击、争吵或强行推进的性质，使他人感到威胁
senses.example: His aggressiveness made every meeting feel like a fight.
senses.exampleCN: 他的好斗让每次开会都像在打架。
senses.why: Aggredi means to step toward someone, and when that step is hostile the -ness noun names a standing readiness to pick a fight.
senses.whyCN: aggredi 意为「朝某人迈步」，当这一步带着敌意时，加 -ness 的名词就表示一种随时准备挑事的常态。

senses.title: Bold drive to win or achieve
senses.definition: the quality of pushing forward confidently and refusing to wait, valued in sport, sales and negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 自信地向前推进、不肯等待的性质，在体育、销售与谈判中受到重视
senses.example: The team lacked the aggressiveness to close the game out.
senses.exampleCN: 这支球队缺少把比赛拿下的那股拼劲。
senses.why: The same forward step is read positively here: nothing changes in the image except whether the observer welcomes the push.
senses.whyCN: 同样是向前迈步，这里被正面解读：画面没有变，变的只是旁观者是否欢迎这一推。

intro.en: Aggressiveness is three layers stacked on a Latin step: ad-, toward, plus gradi, to step, gives aggredi, to approach; -ive turns it into an adjective and -ness into a quality.
intro.cn: aggressiveness 是在拉丁语「迈步」上叠起的三层：ad-「朝向」加 gradi「迈步」构成 aggredi「走近」；-ive 把它变成形容词，-ness 再变成性质名词。

items.en: Latin ad meant to or toward, and it doubles its d to g before a g, giving the spelling aggr-.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ad 意为「向、朝」，在 g 前把 d 同化为 g，于是拼作 aggr-。

items.en: Latin gradi meant to step or walk, the root behind grade, gradual, progress and congress.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，是 grade、gradual、progress 与 congress 背后的词根。

items.en: The deponent verb aggredi meant to approach or to attack, a step taken toward someone with intent.
items.cn: 异态动词 aggredi 意为「走近、攻击」，即带着意图朝某人迈出的一步。

items.en: Late Latin aggressivus described someone given to attacking, built on the past participle aggressus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 aggressivus 描述动辄攻击的人，建立在过去分词 aggressus 之上。

items.en: English took aggressive in the seventeenth century, first of hostile nations and later of forceful salespeople.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 aggressive，先用于敌对国家，后来用于强势的推销员。

items.en: Adding the native suffix -ness produced aggressiveness, now used both of hostility and of praised competitive drive.
items.cn: 加上本族后缀 -ness 得到 aggressiveness，如今既指敌意，也指被称赞的竞争劲头。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the grad- family of stepping; the near-meaning group lists other nouns for a pushing, fighting temperament.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「迈步」的 grad- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「好推进、好斗气质」的名词。

entries.definition: Hostile or violent behaviour toward another.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人怀有敌意或暴力的行为。

entries.definition: Ready to attack, or pushing forward with force.
entries.definitionCN: 随时准备攻击，或强势向前推进。

entries.definition: Forward movement toward a better state.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好状态的向前推进。

entries.definition: To go back to an earlier, worse state.
entries.definitionCN: 退回更早、更差的状态。

entries.definition: Confidence in stating what you want without attacking.
entries.definitionCN: 自信地说出诉求而不攻击他人。

entries.definition: Eager, openly hostile readiness to fight.
entries.definitionCN: 急切而公开敌对的开战意愿。

entries.definition: Unfriendly opposition or dislike.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好的对立或厌恶。

entries.definition: Energy and determination to get things done.
entries.definitionCN: 把事情做成的干劲与决心。

normalIntro.en: Aggressiveness is aggressive plus -ness: the quality of being aggressive, whether that means picking fights or chasing wins.
normalIntro.cn: aggressiveness 就是 aggressive 加 -ness：好斗或敢拼的那种性质，既可能指挑事，也可能指争胜。

normal.en: -ness turns any adjective into a quality: kind gives kindness, aggressive gives aggressiveness.
normal.cn: -ness 把形容词变成性质：kind 变 kindness，aggressive 变 aggressiveness。

normal.en: The double g is ad- meeting gradi, the same doubling you see in aggravate and aggregate.
normal.cn: 双写 g 是 ad- 遇上 gradi，与 aggravate、aggregate 中的双写相同。

normal.en: Aggression is the act; aggressiveness is the habit of doing it.
normal.cn: aggression 是那次行为，aggressiveness 是习惯性地这么做。

normal.en: In sport writing aggressiveness is praise; in a complaint letter it is blame.
normal.cn: 体育报道里 aggressiveness 是褒义，投诉信里则是贬义。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say too much aggressiveness, not many aggressivenesses.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 too much aggressiveness，不说 many aggressivenesses。

abstract.en: Picture a player who lunges at every loose ball before anyone else moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一个球员，每次球一松就抢在所有人之前扑上去。

abstract.en: Imagine two rams butting heads, then the same energy turned into a sales pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象两只公羊顶角，再把同一股劲头变成一段推销说辞。

abstract.en: Think of a spring compressed and ready to push whatever stands in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一根压紧的弹簧，随时准备推开挡在前面的一切。

examples.en: The coach praised the aggressiveness of his young defenders.
examples.cn: 教练称赞了年轻后卫的那股拼劲。

examples.en: Aggressiveness in the interview room can cost you the offer.
examples.cn: 面试时咄咄逼人可能让你丢掉这份工作。

examples.en: They mistook quiet confidence for a lack of aggressiveness.
examples.cn: 他们把沉着的自信误当成缺乏进取心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿哥瑞死我内思」——阿哥（ag-gres）扑过来要死磕（sive），心里（ness）憋着那股劲，就是好斗性、进取劲头。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」在 g 前同化为 ag-，加 gradi「迈步」构成 aggredi「走近、攻击」，其过去分词 aggressus 派生出晚期拉丁语 aggressivus，英语借为 aggressive，再加本族后缀 -ness 构成 aggressiveness，字面即「不断向前迈步的性质」。

sensesIntro.en: One forward push is read two ways: aimed at a person it is hostility, aimed at a goal it is praised drive, and the noun names whichever habit the speaker sees.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一股向前的推力有两种读法：对着人就是敌意，对着目标就是被称赞的干劲，这个名词指的就是说话人看到的那一种习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a force that keeps stepping forward
core.cn: 核心意象：一股不断向前迈步的劲

branches.en: Stepping toward someone to start a quarrel.
branches.cn: 朝某人迈步去挑起争执。

branches.en: A temper that others learn to avoid.
branches.cn: 让别人学会绕着走的脾气。

branches.en: Pressing forward to win a loose ball.
branches.cn: 向前逼抢去争一个松球。

branches.en: Refusing to wait for permission to act.
branches.cn: 不肯等着别人允许才行动。

branches.en: Both name a habit, not a single act.
branches.cn: 两者都指习惯，而非一次行为。

intro.en: Aggressiveness is built in clear layers: a prefix of direction, a root of stepping, an adjective suffix and a native noun suffix.
intro.cn: aggressiveness 的层次非常清楚：方向前缀、迈步词根、形容词后缀，再加本族名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad plus gradi gave aggredi and its participle aggressus; only the final -ness is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad 加 gradi 构成 aggredi 及其分词 aggressus；只有最后的 -ness 是英语本族的。

latinEntries.example: Ad doubles to ag- before g.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ad 在 g 前双写为 ag-。

latinEntries.example: Gradi gives grad- and gress-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: gradi 提供 grad- 与 gress-。

latinEntries.example: Aggredi is the source of aggress-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aggredi 是 aggress- 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Aggressus carries the ss into English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aggressus 把 ss 带进英语。

definition_zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的
definition_en: struck with shock, horror, or amazement
core_image: 血一下子凉透：惊吓从脚底窜上头顶
scene: 拆开信封，账单上的数字让他僵在原地。He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
sceneCN: 这里 aghast 是「惊骇的」（第 1 个义项：被吓到失语僵立）；句意是看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。

pos.zh: 惊骇的；吓呆的（表语用法）

derivatives.zh: 同源日耳曼词 gast 的一支，义为「鬼魂」
ghost 同族形容词，义为「可怕的；苍白的」
aghast 加后缀 -ly（旧式罕用），义为「惊骇地」

senses.title: Struck with shock or horror
senses.definition: filled with sudden shock or terror, often shown by a frozen stare
senses.definitionCN: 充满突如其来的震惊或恐惧，常表现为僵住的凝视
senses.example: He stood aghast at the sum on the final bill.
senses.exampleCN: 看到最终账单上的金额，他惊得僵在原地。
senses.why: The Old English gast meant spirit or breath; to be aghast was to have the breath frightened out of you.

senses.title: Filled with horror at something seen as wrong

senses.definition: shocked by something considered outrageous or unacceptable

senses.example: Readers were aghast that the prize went to a plagiarist.
senses.exampleCN: 奖项颁给了剽窃者，读者们惊骇不已。
senses.why: Horror at danger widened to moral shock: the same frozen breath meets a villain as a ghost.
senses.whyCN: 对危险的恐惧扩大为道义上的震惊：面对恶行与面对鬼魂，同样吓得倒抽冷气。

intro.en: From the past participle of agasten (to frighten), built on Old English gāst (spirit, ghost).
intro.cn: 源自动词 agasten「吓唬」的过去分词，建立在古英语 gāst（灵魂、鬼魂）之上。

items.en: The root *gheys- (to be excited, frightened) underlies gast and ghost.
items.cn: 一般认为词根 *gheys-（激动、惊惧）是 gast 与 ghost 的远源。

items.en: gāst meant breath, spirit, ghost; the verb agāstan meant to terrify.
items.cn: 古英语 gāst 意为「气息、灵魂、鬼魂」，动词 agāstan 意为「使恐惧」。

items.en: agast served as the past participle: frightened out of one's wits.
items.cn: 中古英语 agast 用作过去分词：「被吓得魂不附体」。

items.en: Spelling settled as aghast under the influence of ghost.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪拼写受 ghost 影响定型为 aghast。

items.en: Now almost purely predicative: stand aghast, be aghast at.
items.cn: 如今几乎只作表语：stand aghast、be aghast at。

note.en: Aghast names the frozen face of horror; appalled adds moral outrage, horrified adds fear.
note.cn: aghast 刻画惊骇时僵住的脸；appalled 多一层道义愤怒，horrified 多一层恐惧。

definition_zh: 敏捷的；灵活的；（思维）机敏的
definition_en: able to move quickly and easily; able to think quickly and clearly
core_image: 猫穿屋檐：起步、变向、落地一气呵成
scene: 篮球场上，控卫的变向快得让防守者扑空。The agile guard changed direction so fast that his marker fell away.
sceneCN: 这里 agile 是「身手敏捷的」（第 1 个义项：动作迅速灵活）；句意是控卫变向极快，防守者完全扑空。

pos.zh: 敏捷的；灵活的；机敏的

derivatives.zh: agile 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「敏捷；灵活性」
agile 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「敏捷地」
同根拉丁 agere 一支，义为「代理人；作用者」

senses.title: Able to move quickly and easily
senses.definition: physically quick, light, and well-coordinated in movement
senses.definitionCN: 身体动作迅速、轻巧、协调
senses.example: The agile guard changed direction so fast that his marker fell away.
senses.exampleCN: 控卫变向极快，防守者完全扑空。
senses.why: The Latin agere means to drive, to do; what is agile is ready to act at once, body answering without delay.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 agere 意为「驱动、行动」；agile 之「敏」正是随时可动、身体毫不迟疑地响应。

senses.title: Able to think quickly and clearly
senses.definition: mentally quick, able to grasp and shift ideas without effort
senses.definitionCN: 反应快，能毫不费力地理解并转换思路
senses.example: Her agile mind turned the puzzle inside out within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟内，她就用机敏的头脑把难题翻了个底朝天。
senses.why: A mind that acts the way an agile body does—starting, stopping, turning—is the same quality carried into thought.
senses.whyCN: 头脑像敏捷的身体一样起、停、转向——同一品质移入思维即「机敏」。

senses.title: Adaptable in organization or process
senses.definition: able to change plans quickly in response to new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 能随新情况迅速调整计划与做法
senses.example: Startups survive by staying agile while giants reorganize.
senses.exampleCN: 巨头还在重组，初创公司靠灵活应变活了下来。
senses.why: An institution that moves like an agile body survives change; the bodily image extends to companies and methods.
senses.whyCN: 像敏捷身体一样行动的机构才能应变；身体意象扩展到公司与工作方法。

intro.en: From Latin agilis, from agere (to drive, to do), through French agile into English.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 agilis，出于 agere（驱动、行动），经法语 agile 进入英语。

items.en: The root *h2eg- (to drive, to move) underlies agere and its large family.
items.cn: 一般认为词根 *h2eg-（驱动、移动）是 agere 及其庞大家族的远源。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to act; agilis meant easy to move, nimble.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere 意为「驱动、行动」，agilis 意为「易动的、灵巧的」。

items.en: agile passed through French with the sense of nimble and quick.
items.cn: agile 经法语传入，保留「灵巧、迅捷」之义。

items.en: Borrowed first of bodies, then of minds and wits.
items.cn: 十五世纪借入英语，先指身体，后用于头脑才智。

items.en: The 2001 Agile Manifesto fixed the third sense: adaptive, iterative ways of working.
items.cn: 2001 年《敏捷宣言》确立了第三义：适应性、迭代式的工作方式。

note.en: Agile highlights ease in changing direction; nimble adds lightness, dexterity adds skill of hands.
note.cn: agile 强调变向之自如；nimble 多一层轻巧，dexterity 强调手上的功夫。

definition_zh: 苦苦挣扎；焦虑不安；为（决定）反复纠结；忍受煎熬
definition_en: to spend a long time worrying about a decision or problem without reaching an answer; also to endure prolonged physical or mental pain
core_image: 在赛场上扭着身子较劲，久久分不出胜负
scene: 两份录取通知摊在桌上，她整晚翻来翻去。She agonized over which offer to accept.
sceneCN: 这里 agonize 是「反复纠结、焦虑不安」（第 1 个义项：为某个决定长时间痛苦挣扎）；句意为她整晚为该接受哪份录取而纠结。核心画面是在赛场上扭着身子较劲，久久分不出胜负。

pos.zh: 苦苦挣扎；焦虑不安；久拖不决

derivatives.zh: 英式拼写，与 agonize 同义，义为「苦苦纠结」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人痛苦煎熬的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「令人煎熬地；极其缓慢地」
同根名词，义为「极度痛苦；煎熬」

senses.title: To suffer over a choice
senses.definition: to spend a long time worrying about a decision or a problem, turning it over without reaching an answer
senses.definitionCN: 为某个决定或问题长时间担忧，反复思量却得不到答案
senses.example: He agonized over the wording of a two-line email.
senses.exampleCN: 他为一封两行邮件的措辞纠结了很久。
senses.why: Agon was a contest in which athletes strained against each other, so agonize keeps the picture of an inner match that neither side wins.
senses.whyCN: agon 是运动员彼此较力的竞赛，所以 agonize 保留了一场内心比赛的画面：双方谁也赢不了。

senses.title: To drag on in pain
senses.definition: to endure prolonged physical or mental pain, or to make a process painfully slow, the older and heavier sense
senses.definitionCN: 忍受长时间的身心痛苦，或使某个过程慢得令人难受，是更古老、更沉重的用法
senses.example: The injured runner agonized through the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤的跑者煎熬着跑完最后一圈。
senses.why: Here the contest is against pain itself rather than against a choice, which is exactly how the Greek word was first used.
senses.whyCN: 这里较劲的对手是痛苦本身，而不是某个选择，这正是该希腊词最初的用法。

intro.en: Agonize comes from the Greek games: agon was a contest, agonizesthai was to compete in it, and English turned that public struggle into a private one.
intro.cn: agonize 来自希腊的竞技：agon 是竞赛，agonizesthai 是在其中角逐，英语把这种公开的较劲变成了内心的挣扎。

items.en: Greek agon meant a gathering and then a contest, especially the athletic contests at the great games.
items.cn: 希腊语 agon 先指集会，后指竞赛，尤指大型运动会上的竞技。

items.en: From agon came agonia, the strain of competing, which already covered mental anguish.
items.cn: 由 agon 派生出 agonia，即角逐时的紧绷状态，已涵盖精神上的痛苦。

items.en: The verb agonizesthai meant to contend for a prize, to struggle in the arena.
items.cn: 动词 agonizesthai 意为「争夺奖赏」，即在竞技场上奋力拼搏。

items.en: Late Latin agonizare kept the sense of struggling, and was used of the last struggle before death.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 agonizare 保留「挣扎」之义，并用于指临终前的最后挣扎。

items.en: French agoniser meant to be at the point of death, a narrowing that English later widened again.
items.cn: 法语 agoniser 意为「濒死」，这一收窄后来又被英语重新拓宽。

items.en: English agonize now covers both physical suffering and the everyday torment of choosing, with agonise as the British spelling.
items.cn: 现代英语 agonize 既指身体上的痛苦，也指日常抉择的煎熬，英式拼写作 agonise。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the agon- family of contest and pain; the near-meaning group lists other verbs for worrying at length.
note.cn: 形近组留在表示「竞赛与痛苦」的 agon- 词族内；近义组列出其他表示「长时间担忧」的动词。

entries.definition: Extreme physical or mental suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的身心痛苦。

entries.definition: Causing great pain or anxious delay.
entries.definitionCN: 令人极度痛苦或焦急拖延的。

entries.definition: A person who opposes or competes against another.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人对立或竞争的人。

entries.definition: The leading character in a story or contest.
entries.definitionCN: 故事或竞赛中的主角。

entries.definition: To worry continually about small things.
entries.definitionCN: 为小事不停地烦恼。

entries.definition: To think darkly and at length about something.
entries.definitionCN: 阴郁而长久地想着某事。

entries.definition: To hesitate, unable to decide.
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫不决，拿不定主意。

entries.definition: To struggle with a difficult problem.
entries.definitionCN: 与难题奋力搏斗。

normalIntro.en: Agonize is agon, contest, plus -ize, to act: to keep competing inside your own head.
normalIntro.cn: agonize 就是 agon「竞赛」加 -ize「做……」：在自己脑子里不停地比赛。

normal.en: Agony and agonize share agon, so wherever you see agon- think of a contest that hurts.
normal.cn: agony 与 agonize 共享 agon，所以见到 agon- 就想到一场让人难受的竞赛。

normal.en: Agonize over a choice, agonize about a situation: over points at the thing you must pick.
normal.cn: agonize over 后接要挑的东西，agonize about 后接让人担忧的处境。

normal.en: American spelling ends in -ize, British in -ise: agonize and agonise are the same verb.
normal.cn: 美式拼写以 -ize 结尾，英式以 -ise 结尾：agonize 与 agonise 是同一个动词。

normal.en: The -ing form works as an adjective, as in an agonizing wait.
normal.cn: -ing 形式可作形容词，如 an agonizing wait（煎熬的等待）。

normal.en: It is usually intransitive, so say agonize over it, not agonize it.
normal.cn: 它通常不及物，所以说 agonize over it，不说 agonize it。

abstract.en: Picture two wrestlers locked in your chest, neither able to pin the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个摔跤手在你胸口僵持，谁也压不倒谁。

abstract.en: Imagine a stadium where the only event is deciding, and it never ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，唯一的项目是「做决定」，而且永不结束。

abstract.en: Think of a clock whose hands move only while you worry.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，只有在你担忧时指针才走动。

examples.en: She agonized for weeks before handing in her resignation.
examples.cn: 她纠结了好几个星期才递交辞呈。

examples.en: Do not agonize over a sentence nobody will read twice.
examples.cn: 别为一个没人会读第二遍的句子反复纠结。

examples.en: The whole family agonized while the results were pending.
examples.cn: 结果未定的那段时间，全家人都在煎熬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱哥奈兹」——爱（a）哥（go）奈（n）兹（ize）：心里两个小人比赛，谁也不服谁，就是苦苦纠结、焦虑不安。

root: 希腊语 agon「集会、竞赛」派生出 agonia「角逐的紧绷」与 agonizesthai「争夺奖赏」，经晚期拉丁语 agonizare「挣扎」与法语 agoniser「濒死」进入英语，加动词后缀 -ize 构成 agonize，字面即「像竞技一样持续较劲」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are a contest that will not end: in one you wrestle with a choice, in the other with pain, and in each the struggle itself is the point.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是一场不肯结束的竞赛：一个与选择较劲，一个与痛苦较劲，两者都以「挣扎本身」为重点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner contest with no winner
core.cn: 核心意象：一场分不出胜负的内心竞赛

branches.en: Turning a choice over all night.
branches.cn: 整晚把一个选择翻来覆去地想。

branches.en: Rewriting one sentence again and again.
branches.cn: 把一句话改了一遍又一遍。

branches.en: Pushing through pain to finish.
branches.cn: 忍着痛苦坚持到结束。

branches.en: A wait that feels longer than the clock says.
branches.cn: 一段比钟表所示更漫长的等待。

branches.en: Both keep the struggle going without a result.
branches.cn: 两者都让挣扎持续而没有结果。

intro.en: Agonize belongs to the agon- family, where the root always names a contest and the suffix decides whether you get a noun, a verb or an adjective.
intro.cn: agonize 属于 agon- 词族，词根永远表示竞赛，后缀决定你得到的是名词、动词还是形容词。

latinIntro.en: Greek agon passed through late Latin agonizare and French agoniser before English added the verb suffix -ize.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 agon 经晚期拉丁语 agonizare 与法语 agoniser，再由英语加上动词后缀 -ize。

latinEntries.example: Agon is the root of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agon 是整个词族的词根。

latinEntries.example: Agonia already meant anguish.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agonia 已表示痛苦。

latinEntries.example: Agonizesthai lies behind agonize.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agonizesthai 是 agonize 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Agonizare carried the word into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: agonizare 把该词带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 土地的；农业的；农村的；（名词）主张土地改革者
definition_en: relating to land, its ownership and its cultivation, or to the rural order built on it
core_image: 一张地契压在木桌上，旁边是犁、界石与一小袋谷种
scene: 村公所的抽屉里放着几份旧地契，田界用石头标着。Land disputes in the valley are settled by agrarian law that dates back centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 agrarian 指「与土地及其占有关系有关的」（第 1 个义项：土地与土地占有的）；句意为这个河谷的土地纠纷依数百年前传下的土地法解决。图中可辨识物件：地契、木桌、犁、界石、谷种。

主张土地改革者；平均地权论者

senses.title: Of land and its ownership
senses.definition: relating to land as property, especially to who owns and who works it
senses.definitionCN: 与作为财产的土地有关，尤其涉及谁拥有、谁耕作
senses.example: Land disputes in the valley are settled by agrarian law that dates back centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河谷的土地纠纷依数百年前传下的土地法解决。
senses.why: the word comes from the Latin word for field, so its core is land as an object held and divided.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示田地的词，因此其核心是作为被占有、被分割之物的土地。

senses.title: Of farming as a way of life
senses.titleCN: 作为一种生活方式的农耕
senses.definition: relating to the practice and rhythm of cultivating the soil
senses.definitionCN: 与耕作土地的实践和节奏有关
senses.example: The museum records the agrarian year from ploughing to threshing.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了从犁地到脱粒的农事一年。
senses.why: owning land and working it are two sides of the same order, so the adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 拥有土地与耕作土地是同一秩序的两面，因此这个形容词两者都涵盖。

senses.title: Of land redistribution
senses.definition: used of reforms that change who holds land, often breaking up large estates
senses.definitionCN: 用于改变土地持有者的改革，常拆散大庄园
senses.example: Agrarian reform gave tenants title to the fields they farmed.
senses.exampleCN: 土地改革把佃农所耕田地的产权给了他们。
senses.why: if land is the basis of power, then changing its ownership is the central political demand of the word.
senses.whyCN: 如果土地是权力基础，那么改变其所有权就是这个词的核心政治诉求。

senses.title: Of a rural social order
senses.titleCN: 农村社会秩序意义上的
senses.definition: describing societies or economies organized around land, villages and rural classes
senses.definitionCN: 描述围绕土地、村落与农村阶级组织起来的社会或经济
senses.example: The region remained agrarian long after the coast industrialized.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海工业化很久之后，这个地区仍以农业为主。
senses.why: the adjective can describe a whole order, not only a single plot or law.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以描述整个秩序，而不只是单块土地或单条法律。

senses.title: A land-reform advocate
senses.definition: a person who campaigns for a fairer distribution of land
senses.definitionCN: 为更公平的土地分配而奔走的人
senses.example: The agrarian spoke at every village meeting that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天，这位土地改革者在每次村会上发言。
senses.why: the adjective became a noun for the person who carries its political programme.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转为名词，指承载其政治纲领的人。

senses.title: Roman land law
senses.definition: the body of ancient Roman laws about the division and use of public land
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马关于公地分配与使用的法律体系
senses.example: The agrarian laws limited how much public land one family could hold.
senses.exampleCN: 土地法限制一个家庭能占有的公地上限。
senses.why: the phrase is fixed in Roman history, where land division was a standing political conflict.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法在罗马史中固定下来，因为土地分配是长期的政治冲突。

senses.title: Of a farmed landscape
senses.definition: describing a landscape or ecology shaped by centuries of cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 描述被数百年耕作塑造的景观或生态
senses.example: The agrarian landscape of hedges and terraces supports many species.
senses.exampleCN: 由树篱与梯田构成的农耕景观养活了众多物种。
senses.why: land that has been worked for generations becomes a visible pattern, and the adjective names that pattern.
senses.whyCN: 被世代耕作的土地会成为可见的图案，这个形容词命名那种图案。

senses.title: Of rural unrest
senses.definition: describing conflict or crisis rooted in land hunger and tenure
senses.definitionCN: 描述源于土地饥渴与占有关系的冲突或危机
senses.example: The agrarian crisis drove thousands off the land and into the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 农业危机把成千上万人赶离土地、涌入城市。
senses.why: when tenure is unjust or unviable, the same word shifts from description to the name of a crisis.
senses.whyCN: 当土地占有不公或难以为继时，同一个词便从描述转为危机之名。

intro.en: Agrarian comes from Latin agrarius 'of land', built on ager 'field'. English adopted it in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: agrarian 来自拉丁 agrarius「土地的」，由 ager「田地」构成。英语在 16 世纪吸收这个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, farmland, territory'. It also gives acre; its Indo-European source is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、耕地、领地」，也构成 acre；其印欧来源属重构形式，而非有据可查的材料。

items.en: Agrarius meant 'of fields, relating to land', and was used of laws about public land and of the men who proposed them.
items.cn: agrarius 意为「田地的、与土地有关的」，用于关于公地的法律，也用于提出这些法律的人。

items.en: The leges agrariae of the Roman republic divided public land and limited holdings, which fixed the political sense of the word.
items.cn: 罗马共和国的土地法分配公地并限制占有上限，这固定了这个词的政治含义。

items.en: English took agrarian in the sixteenth century for matters of land and tenure, and later widened it to whole rural orders.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪吸收 agrarian，用于土地与占有事务，后来扩大到整个农村秩序。

items.en: Nineteenth-century land reform movements made the word a programme as well as a description, and its noun named the advocate.
items.cn: 19 世纪的土地改革运动使这个词既是描述也是纲领，其名词形式则指主张者。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin root of ager is a reconstruction, and the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：ager 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，最早的英语书证也没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the land-family words that are most often confused; group two holds near neighbours of rural life.
note.cn: 第一组是最易混淆的土地词族成员；第二组是农村生活的近邻说法。

entries.definition: Of farming technique and production; it describes how food is grown, while agrarian describes land tenure and the rural order.
entries.definitionCN: 指农耕技术与生产；描述粮食如何种植，而土地一词描述土地占有与农村秩序。

entries.definition: The science of crop production and soil management; a technical field, not a social order.
entries.definitionCN: 作物生产与土壤管理的科学；属技术领域，不是社会秩序。

entries.definition: A unit of land area; it descends from the same word for field but names a measure, not a social question.
entries.definitionCN: 土地面积单位；与田地一词同源，但指度量，不指社会问题。

entries.definition: To convert land or a community to small-scale farming; rare and technical, unlike the everyday adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地或社群转为小农耕种；罕用且技术化，不同于日常形容词。

entries.definition: Of the countryside; it describes location and population density rather than land ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 乡村的；描述地点与人口密度，而非土地占有。

entries.definition: Of shepherds and grazing, and also of an idealized country life; it is not about crops or tenure.
entries.definitionCN: 牧人与放牧的，也指理想化的乡野生活；与作物或土地占有无关。

entries.definition: Describing people or families that own substantial land; it names the proprietor rather than the order.
entries.definitionCN: 描述拥有大量土地的人或家族；命名的是所有者而非秩序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means field, so agrarian is about land before it is about crops.
normal.cn: 词根意为田地，因此土地先于作物。

normal.en: Agrarian reform is the fixed phrase that shows the political sense.
normal.cn: 土地改革这一固定搭配展示了政治义。

normal.en: The pair agrarian and agricultural divides ownership from technique.
normal.cn: 土地的一词与农业的一词，把占有与技术分开。

normal.en: Roman agrarian laws are the historical anchor of the word.
normal.cn: 罗马土地法是这个词的历史锚点。

normal.en: As a noun it names the person who campaigns for land reform.
normal.cn: 作名词时，它指为土地改革奔走的人。

abstract.en: Picture a deed lying on a table beside a plough.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地契放在桌上，旁边是一把犁。

abstract.en: Picture a boundary stone that outlasts the families who argued over it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块界石比争它的人家存续得更久。

abstract.en: Picture a field divided by lines that only the law can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田被只有法律看得见的线分割。

examples.en: Agrarian reform was the central issue of the election.
examples.cn: 土地改革是这次选举的核心议题。

examples.en: The agrarian economy depended on one harvest a year.
examples.cn: 农业经济一年只依赖一次收成。

examples.en: Agrarian unrest followed the rise in rents.
examples.cn: 地租上涨之后出现了农村动荡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「土地（agrarian）」——与田地、地契和界石打交道的，就是土地的、农业的

root: 拉丁 ager「田地」→ agrarius「土地的」→ 英语 agrarian。ager 的更深词根属重构形式；同源词包括 acre。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plot of ground: land as property, farming as a way of life, redistribution, the rural order, the advocate, Roman land law, the farmed landscape and the unrest that tenure can cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一块地面展开：作为财产的土地、作为生活方式的农耕、土地再分配、农村秩序、主张改革的人、罗马土地法、被耕作塑造的景观，以及占有关系可能引发的动荡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deed, a plough, a boundary stone and a bag of seed on one table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上放着地契、犁、界石与一袋谷种。

branches.en: PROPERTY: the base sense, land as something owned and divided.
branches.cn: 财产：基础义，作为被占有、被分割之物的土地。

branches.en: WORK AND LANDSCAPE: cultivation as a way of life, and the visible pattern it leaves.
branches.cn: 劳作与景观：作为生活方式的耕作，以及它留下的可见图案。

branches.en: REDISTRIBUTION: reform as a programme, and the advocate who carries it.
branches.cn: 再分配：作为纲领的改革，以及承载它的主张者。

branches.en: ORDER AND LAW: the rural order in general, and the Roman laws that fixed the term.
branches.cn: 秩序与法律：一般的农村秩序，以及固定这个术语的罗马法律。

branches.en: CONFLICT: when tenure fails, the same adjective names a crisis.
branches.cn: 冲突：当占有关系难以为继，同一个形容词成为危机之名。

intro.en: Agrarian is a Latin root plus an adjective suffix, and the root also yields agriculture and acre.
intro.cn: agrarian 由一个拉丁词根加一个形容词后缀构成，这个词根还给出 agriculture 与 acre。

latinIntro.en: Latin ager 'field' gives agrarius and agrarian, and through cultura it also gives agriculture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ager「田地」给出 agrarius 与 agrarian，并经 cultura 给出 agriculture。

items.example: The root names the ground itself.
It turns the land root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把土地词根变成形容词。

items.example: It names the political programme of land reform.
items.exampleCN: 它命名土地改革的政治纲领。

items.meaningCN: 土地改革主义；农本主义
items.example: Agrarianism spread among the tenant farmers.
items.exampleCN: 农本主义在佃农中传播。

items.example: It forms the rare verb of conversion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成罕用的转换动词。

items.example: The board agrarianized the estate after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后委员会把这片庄园改为小农耕种。

definition_zh: 农业的；农学的；耕种的；农田的
definition_en: relating to farming, to the science of farming, or to land used for growing crops
core_image: 犁铧翻开泥土，一条直直的垄沟伸向远处
scene: 天还没亮，收割机就开进了麦田，车灯照着一行行麦茬。The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 agricultural 是「农业的」（第 1 个义项：与耕作、畜牧相关的）；句意为这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。

pos.zh: 形容词：农业的；农学的；耕种的

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「农业；农学」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在农业方面」
由本词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「农学家；务农者」

senses.title: Relating to farming
senses.definition: relating to the growing of crops and the raising of animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 与种植作物、饲养食用动物相关的
senses.example: The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the whole activity of farming to any noun that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把耕作这一整件事附加到它后面的名词上。

senses.title: Relating to the science of farming
senses.definition: relating to the academic study of farming methods and soils
senses.definitionCN: 与农作方法与土壤的学术研究相关的
senses.example: She is doing agricultural research on drought-resistant wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做抗旱小麦的农业研究。
senses.why: Once farming becomes a subject taught in universities, its adjective also names the research side.
senses.whyCN: 一旦耕作成为大学里讲授的学科，这个形容词也用来指研究的那一面。

senses.title: Involving cultivation of the soil
senses.definition: involving the actual tilling and working of land
senses.definitionCN: 涉及实际翻耕与打理土地的
senses.example: Most families here have an agricultural life rather than an industrial one.
senses.exampleCN: 这里多数家庭过的是务农生活，而不是工业生活。
senses.why: Latina cultura meant tending, and the adjective keeps that hands-in-the-soil sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cultura 意为「照料」，这个形容词保留了双手沾泥的那层意思。

senses.title: Of land used for crops
senses.definition: describing land or areas set aside for crops or pasture
senses.definitionCN: 描述专门用于种植或放牧的土地与区域
senses.example: Half of the region is agricultural land and the rest is forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区一半是农田，其余是森林。
senses.why: Land itself can be labelled by what it is used for, so the adjective moves from activity to territory.
senses.whyCN: 土地本身可以按用途被命名，于是这个形容词从活动转到了地界。

intro.en: Agricultural is an English adjective on agriculture, whose two Latin halves mean field and tending.
intro.cn: agricultural 是在 agriculture 之上构成的英语形容词，而后者的两个拉丁成分意为「田地」与「照料」。

items.en: Ager meant a field or open land, and it is the first half of the word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ager 意为「田地、开阔地」，是这个词的前半。

items.en: Cultura meant tending, cultivation, and later also the training of mind; here it keeps the farming sense.
items.cn: cultura 意为「照料、耕作」，后来也指心智的培养；在此保留农耕义。

items.en: The compound agricultura named the cultivation of fields, and English took it as agriculture in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 agricultura 指田地的耕作，英语十六世纪借入为 agriculture。

items.en: The adjective agricultural was formed with -al as farming became a subject of policy and science. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 随着农业成为政策与科学研究的对象，形容词 agricultural 由 -al 构成。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The adjective now covers farming as work, as science, and as a use of land.
items.cn: 如今这个形容词覆盖农业作为劳动、作为科学，以及作为土地用途三个方面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the agriculture family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for country life and cultivation.
note.cn: 形近组是 agriculture 词族；近义组收描述乡村生活与耕作的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for farming and for the science that studies it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农业、农学」，是本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in farming terms or from a farming point of view.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在农业方面」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises farming as a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农学家、务农者」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Relating to land ownership and rural society, rather than to farming technique.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土地的、农耕社会的」，侧重土地制度而非耕作技术。

entries.definition: Relating to the countryside, including villages and life outside cities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乡村的」，涵盖村庄与城市之外的生活。

entries.definition: The everyday noun and modifier for the work of growing crops and keeping animals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词兼修饰语，义为「务农、耕作」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to garden cultivation, a narrower field than agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「园艺的」，范围比农业更窄，专指园圃栽培。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin halves of the word and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的两个拉丁成分，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ager is a field and cultura is tending, so agricultural means field-tending.
normal.cn: ager 是田地，cultura 是照料，所以 agricultural 就是「照料田地」。

normal.en: Agriculture is the noun; agricultural is what you call anything that belongs to it.
normal.cn: agriculture 是名词；凡属于它的事物，就用 agricultural 来形容。

normal.en: Agricultural land is land earmarked for crops or pasture.
normal.cn: agricultural land 是划给作物或牧场的土地。

normal.en: Agricultural science is the university side of the same activity.
normal.cn: agricultural science 是同一件事在大学里的那一面。

normal.en: Cultura also gives culture, which is the tending of minds instead of fields.
normal.cn: cultura 还生出 culture，那是照料心智而非田地。

abstract.en: Picture a plough blade opening the soil and a straight furrow running to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象犁铧翻开泥土，一条笔直的垄沟伸向天边。

abstract.en: Follow the furrow and it passes a laboratory, a policy office, and a land register.
abstract.cn: 沿着这条垄沟走，它会经过一间实验室、一个政策办公室和一本土地登记册。

abstract.en: The same line is work, study and territory at once.
abstract.cn: 同一条线同时是劳动、学问与地界。

examples.en: The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
examples.cn: 这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。

examples.en: Half of the region is agricultural land and the rest is forest.
examples.cn: 这个地区一半是农田，其余是森林。

examples.en: She is doing agricultural research on drought-resistant wheat.
examples.cn: 她在做抗旱小麦的农业研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿哥，犁扣」——阿哥把犁扣在田里：农业的

root: 拉丁语 ager「田地」加 cultura「照料、耕作」构成 agricultura「耕作田地」，英语十六世纪借入为 agriculture，十八世纪再加形容词后缀 -al 构成 agricultural；cultura 也是 culture 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses apply one adjective to four sides of the same activity: the work itself, the science of it, the labour of tilling, and the land it uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项把同一个形容词用到同一件事的四个侧面：农活本身、研究它的学问、翻土劳作，以及它所占的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plough blade opens the soil and a straight furrow runs towards the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：犁铧翻开泥土，一条笔直的垄沟伸向天边。

branches.en: THE WORK: the adjective names everything that belongs to growing crops and keeping animals.
branches.cn: 劳动线：这个形容词指一切与种植和饲养相关的事物。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same activity becomes a university subject with its own research.
branches.cn: 学问线：同一件事变成大学里的一门学科，拥有自己的研究。

branches.en: THE HANDS: cultura keeps the sense of actual tending, hands in the soil.
branches.cn: 双手线：cultura 保留实际照料的意思，双手沾着泥土。

branches.en: THE GROUND: land is labelled by the use it is put to.
branches.cn: 土地线：土地按用途被命名。

branches.en: THE BASE: both rest on the same Latin pair, field plus tending.
branches.cn: 根基线：两者都建立在同一对拉丁成分上，即田地加照料。

intro.en: Agricultural combines a Latin compound noun with the English adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: agricultural 把拉丁复合名词与英语形容词后缀 -al 组合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Ager, cultura and agricultura are all recorded, so nothing in this entry is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ager、cultura 与 agricultura 均有记录，本条目的成分都不是重构形式。

items.example: Ager is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ager 是这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Cultura also gives the English word culture.
items.exampleCN: cultura 还生出英语词 culture。

items.example: It appears in agronomy and agrochemical.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 agronomy 与 agrochemical 中。

items.example: The map marks all agricultural land in green.
items.exampleCN: 地图把农业用地都标成绿色。

由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「在农业方面」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「农学家」
